providers.description: Amphenol is one of the world's largest designers, manufacturers, and marketers of electrical, electronic, and fiber optic connectors, interconnect systems, antennas, sensors, and cables used across military-aerospace, industrial, automotive, information technology, mobile phones, wireless infrastructure, broadband, medical device, and professional audio markets worldwide.

providers.name: Hireology
providers.description: Hireology is a purpose-built applicant tracking system (ATS) and hiring platform for multi-location, high-volume employers, with deep specialization in retail automotive, healthcare (including long-term and home care), and hospitality. The platform spans the full hiring lifecycle — candidate sourcing and job distribution, applicant engagement and texting, structured screening and skills assessments, interview and evaluation workflows, hiring decisions, and onboarding handoff — plus reporting and analytics that help operators hire consistently, faster, and at scale across locations. Hireology integrates with payroll, HRIS, background-check, scheduling, and job-board partners such as ADP, UKG, BambooHR, Indeed, CDK, Dealertrack, and Accurate. It maintains a SOC 2 Type II program and a public Trust Center. Hireology does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI specification; integrations are delivered through named partner connectors. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Lendbuzz
providers.description: Lendbuzz is a Boston-headquartered auto finance platform, founded in 2015, that uses machine learning and alternative data — bank transaction history, education, employment and income signals rather than a traditional FICO file — to underwrite consumers with thin or no US credit history. The company originates retail auto loans through a nationwide network of franchise and independent dealerships, and also provides dealers with floor planning and an AI-assisted "Express Contract" digital contracting flow. Dealers submit and manage deals through the Lendbuzz Dealer Portal at app.lendbuzz.com, or by routing credit applications through the Dealertrack and RouteOne F&I networks; consumers use a separate Client Portal. Lendbuzz Funding, LLC is a licensed lender (NMLS ID #1636296) and funds originations through recurring asset-backed securitizations. As of this profiling pass Lendbuzz publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract — partner integration is intermediated by Dealertrack and RouteOne.

providers.name: Kleio
providers.description: Kleio is a Paris-headquartered agentic commerce platform for complex, high-value enterprise sales, founded in 2024 by Adrien Mathieu, Philippe Wellens and Louis Poirier and backed by a EUR 3M seed round. The platform pairs a domain-specific Knowledge Engine — a continuously updated representation of a company's catalog, pricing, business rules and ontologies — with a stack of orchestrated AI agents tuned for each stage of the sales funnel: discovery agents for intent qualification, product-guidance agents that reason over the catalog, quoting agents wired to configurators and pricing, and a Live Sales Copilot that augments human advisors in real time. Kleio deploys across web widgets, advisor desktops and third-party AI surfaces such as ChatGPT and Gemini via MCP/UCP integrations, with CRM and catalog write-back to Salesforce, HubSpot and custom systems. Named customers include Selectour, Havas Voyages, Showroomprive, Altarea Cogedim, Orpi and Emil Frey, across travel, real estate, automotive, wholesale, insurance, manufacturing and energy. Kleio publishes no public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI: the platform API at api.kleio.ai is an OAuth-protected Google Cloud API Gateway reachable only to customers, and access begins with a sales conversation.

providers.name: Polaris Industries
providers.description: Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII), long known as Polaris Industries, is a Minnesota-based global manufacturer of powersports and off-road vehicles. Its portfolio spans RANGER, RZR, Polaris XPEDITION and GENERAL side-by-sides, Sportsman ATVs, snowmobiles, Slingshot moto-roadsters, military and commercial off-road vehicles, Aixam quadricycles, Goupil electric utility vehicles, and Bennington and Godfrey pontoon and deck boats. Its connected-vehicle platform, RIDE COMMAND, ships in-dash navigation and vehicle telematics to riders as an end-user product. Polaris completed the separation of Indian Motorcycle and the sale of a majority stake to Carolwood LP on 2 February 2026. Polaris publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; the only credentialed integration surface a member of the public can find is the dealer portal at polarisportal.com, which authenticates against an Auth0 tenant.

providers.name: Subaru of America
providers.description: Subaru of America, Inc. is the United States subsidiary of Subaru Corporation (Japan), headquartered in Camden, New Jersey. SOA sells, services, and supports the Subaru lineup through more than 600 U.S. dealers and operates the MySubaru / STARLINK connected-vehicle platform that powers the MySubaru mobile app, owner portal, remote vehicle commands, safety and security services, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, and dealer integration. None of these surfaces are exposed as a public developer API; all known interfaces are private, OEM-internal, or partner-only.

providers.name: Dealertrack
providers.description: Dealertrack is a Cox Automotive brand providing automotive dealership software - a cloud-based Dealer Management System (DMS), digital contracting and F&I tools, and the largest dealer-to-lender credit application network in the United States. Its developer surface is partner-gated. Dealership systems integrate through the Opentrack third-party integration program (real-time, bidirectional REST access to DMS data such as vehicles, customers, deals, repair orders, parts, and general ledger) and through the Cox Automotive Integration Platform partner storefront at developer.coxautoinc.com (OAuth-secured, partner onboarding required). Dealertrack publishes no open, self-service public API; access requires Opentrack certification and annual fees, integration through a certified Opentrack partner, or a Cox Automotive partner agreement. The endpoints described here are modeled from public product and program documentation, not from an open API reference.

providers.name: Automotive Grade Linux
providers.description: Automotive Grade Linux (AGL) is a collaborative open source project under the Linux Foundation that develops a unified software platform for connected vehicles. AGL brings together automakers (Toyota, Honda, Mercedes-Benz), suppliers, and technology companies to build an open Linux-based software stack for in-vehicle infotainment, instrument clusters, telematics, and software-defined vehicle (SoDeV) architectures. The platform decouples software from hardware enabling rapid automotive application development.

providers.name: Arconic
providers.description: Arconic Corporation is an aluminum solutions company producing rolled aluminum sheet and plate, extrusions, and architectural building products for the aerospace, automotive, commercial transportation, building & construction, industrial, and packaging markets. Spun off from Alcoa in 2016, separated from Howmet Aerospace in 2020, and acquired by Apollo Global Management in August 2023 for approximately $5.2 billion, Arconic now operates as a private company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Key brands include Kawneer architectural systems and Reynobond aluminum composite panels.

providers.name: Mihup
providers.description: Mihup is an enterprise Voice AI and speech analytics platform founded in 2016 and headquartered in Kolkata, India. Its full-stack voice AI (ASR, NLU, TTS, analytics) powers four products: Interaction Analytics (MIA) for 100% call auditing, Voice Agent (MVA) for inbound/outbound call automation, Agent Assist (MAA) for real-time live-agent guidance, and Automotive Voice Agent (AVA) for in-car assistants in software-defined vehicles. Proprietary phoneme-based (G2P) recognition supports 120+ languages, accents and dialects including 20+ Indian languages and code-mixed Hinglish. Mihup runs in 1.5M+ cars, processes 5M+ interactions daily, and is trusted by 500+ businesses including Tata Motors, SBI Life and IDFC FIRST Bank. ISO 27001 certified, DPDP Act 2023 and RBI data-localization compliant, hosted in AWS Mumbai. Mihup exposes APIs and SDKs for IVI systems, chipsets, telecom stacks and CRMs, but publishes no public developer portal — access is enterprise/demo-gated.

providers.name: Breathe Battery Technologies
providers.description: Breathe Battery Technologies is a UK battery software company, spun out of Imperial College London in 2019, that builds physics-based battery simulation, cell design, and adaptive charging software for OEM and cell engineering teams. Its API-delivered products — Breathe Design (cell design), Breathe Simulate (validated performance and degradation modelling), and Breathe Charge (embedded adaptive charging, shipped in Volvo EVs) — are consumed through first-party Python client libraries (breathe-simulate, breathe-design) and MATLAB/Simulink integration, backed by a token-authenticated cloud service. The company is venture-backed (Speedinvest among its investors) and profiled in the API Evangelist network for its developer-facing, programmatically accessible battery engineering platform.

providers.name: Rush Enterprises
providers.description: Rush Enterprises is the largest network of commercial vehicle dealerships in North America, operating Rush Truck Centers with more than 200 locations across the United States. The company offers new and used commercial vehicles, all-makes parts, vehicle technology solutions, collision repair, alternative fuel systems, vehicle and equipment leasing, and financial services. Rush Enterprises provides fleet technology through RushCare, including Service Connect (integrated with OEMs like Peterbilt, International, Hino, and Cummins), Parts Connect, and telematics solutions powered by Geotab.

providers.name: Reed Semiconductor
providers.description: Reed Semiconductor Corp. is a fabless power-management semiconductor company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Rhode Island, USA, with offices in Taipei, Shenzhen and Bengaluru. The name stands for Robust, Efficient, Eco-friendly and Dense power solutions. It designs multiphase DC-DC controllers, smart power stages, half-bridge power stages, point-of-load converters, power modules, intermediate bus converters, eFuses and power multiplexers for data center and AI/HPC accelerators, 48V and 12V distribution, communication and datacom equipment, automotive ADAS and infotainment, industrial systems and personal electronics. Reed does not operate a developer program, but its WordPress/WooCommerce corporate site exposes real machine-readable surfaces: an anonymous WooCommerce Store API serving the 99-part parametric product catalog across 81 application and technology categories, the WordPress content API, and an OAuth 2.1 protected Model Context Protocol server published through RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata at the apex domain.

providers.name: AramisAuto
providers.description: Aramisauto is the French retail brand of Aramis Group (Euronext Paris: ARAMI, majority-owned by Stellantis), founded in 2001 by Nicolas Chartier and Guillaume Paoli. It sells used, 0km and new cars online as a mandataire, reconditions vehicles in its own refurbishing centres, runs a trade-in service ("reprise") that pays within 24 hours, and arranges financing (crédit, LOA, LLD) through Cetelem, Socram, PSA Banque, Lizauto and Opteven. Aramisauto operates no public developer programme: there is no portal, no OpenAPI and no SDK. What it does publish is machine-readable and first-party — ten JSON Schema 2020-12 contracts at schemas.aramis.group covering the vehicle catalog (search request/response, the multi-language ingest model, the single-language read model served from "the preheated cache for the APIs", and the search-index projection) plus the four-stage collect/map/filter/enrich configuration contracts third-party marketplace sellers are onboarded with — and an llms.txt at the site root. Its API vhost, api.aramisauto.com, answers every anonymous request with an HTTP 403 demanding a WSSE (WS-Security UsernameToken) credential.

providers.name: Upstream Security
providers.description: Upstream Security is a cloud-based automotive and smart-mobility cybersecurity company. Its purpose-built vehicle data platform delivers Cyber XDR detection and response for connected vehicles, runtime AI and API security, proactive quality detection, and advanced analytics, alongside AutoThreat PRO threat intelligence and Vehicle Security Operations Center (vSOC) services for OEMs, Tier 1 and 2 suppliers, fleets, insurers, EV charging, and mobility IoT operators. Upstream publishes no public developer portal or API; the platform is sold as enterprise SaaS with demo-based onboarding.

providers.name: Mitchell 1
providers.description: Mitchell 1 is a division of Snap-on Incorporated providing repair information (ProDemand, TruckSeries) and shop management software (Manager SE, SocialCRM) to independent auto repair shops. Mitchell 1 is a legacy enterprise software provider, not an API-first company - it has no public, self-serve REST API reference. It does operate a gated Web-Intent / Data API integration program for approved third-party partners (shop management systems, CRM, parts and marketing platforms) to embed or link into ProDemand labor, parts, and maintenance data, fronted by a token-based (TAPE) auth flow and an Intent Registry discovery service. Access requires submitting an integration request, a Mitchell 1 review (roughly two weeks), and a signed partner agreement; no public API reference, OpenAPI document, or SDK is published. Note - Mitchell 1 (mitchell1.com, Snap-on) is a distinct company from Mitchell International (mitchell.com, part of Enlyte) - the two share a historical "Mitchell" lineage but are separately owned; Mitchell International's public developer.mitchell.com RepairCenter API belongs to the other company and is out of scope here.

providers.name: Vishay Intertechnology
providers.description: Vishay Intertechnology is one of the world's largest manufacturers of discrete semiconductors (diodes, rectifiers, MOSFETs, optoelectronics, selected ICs) and passive electronic components (resistors, inductors, capacitors). Vishay components are used in automotive, industrial, computing, consumer, telecommunications, military, aerospace, and medical applications. Component data is accessible via distributor APIs (Octopart/Nexar, DigiKey) and Vishay's own Parts Library (VPL) tool.

providers.name: Revion
providers.description: Revion builds an AI-powered operating system for automotive retail service operations. Its voice-first platform lets dealership technicians dictate repair information hands-free, automatically structuring their speech into repair orders, multi-point inspections, and service recommendations in real time so shops can service more vehicles and capture more high-margin work. Revion is a Winter 2026 Y Combinator company based in New York City, operating across US and EU regions. As of this profile Revion is an early-stage product company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this entry captures its public identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CarMax
providers.description: CarMax (NYSE: KMX) is the largest retailer of used cars in the United States, operating an omnichannel business that spans brick-and-mortar stores, carmax.com online purchasing, home delivery, financing, appraisals, and trade-ins. CarMax does not publish a public developer portal, but its engineering organization operates an extensive internal API program built around distinct API roles (Data Access Layer, Business Logic Layer, Server-Driven UI, Backend for Frontend). Public-facing APIs documented by the CarMax Engineering Blog include a Store Locations API and a Vehicle Inventory API, and CarMax has publicly discussed a Server-Driven UI API that controls vehicle search filters across web and mobile. Partner and syndication integrations are handled case by case rather than through a self-service portal.

providers.name: Snap-on
providers.description: Snap-on Incorporated is a global manufacturer and marketer of tools, equipment, diagnostics, repair information, and systems solutions for professional users in vehicle repair, industrial, and other industries. The company provides diagnostic tools, electronic parts catalogs (EPC), repair information systems (ShopKey Pro, SureTrack), and shop management software. Snap-on integrates with dealer management systems (DMS) through its EPC integration program and strategic technology partnerships.

providers.name: SPREAD
providers.description: SPREAD is a Berlin-based, AI-native engineering intelligence platform for complex product development and manufacturing. It connects fragmented product lifecycle data across PLM, CAD, ERP, requirements, and simulation systems into a unified engineering ontology, so teams building automotive, defense, and industrial products can find issues earlier and ship faster. The platform surfaces a set of engineering intelligence solutions — Requirements Manager, Product Explorer, Error Inspector, and Action Tower — on top of SPREAD Studio, a low-code environment for building custom analyses, with 40+ connectors to systems such as Teamcenter, Windchill, 3DEXPERIENCE, SAP, Polarion, JIRA, CATIA, and Creo. Customers include Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Ford, Bosch, Audi, and Daimler Truck. Backed by HV Capital; added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: OLX
providers.description: OLX is a global online classifieds and marketplace operator, part of OLX Group (owned by Prosus / Naspers), running consumer buy-and-sell marketplaces across 30+ countries under 20+ brands including OLX Poland (olx.pl), OLX Brazil (olx.com.br), OLX Portugal, OLX Bulgaria and OLX Romania, spanning general classifieds, motors/autos, and real estate. OLX Poland publishes a public Partner API (OAuth2) that lets integrators and sellers manage adverts, categories/attributes, and delivery settings programmatically. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tenneco
providers.description: Tenneco is a global manufacturer of automotive components and systems, including clean air, powertrain, and ride performance systems for OEM and aftermarket markets. Through its DRiV aftermarket division, Tenneco serves mechanics, distributors, and retailers with digital catalog and parts lookup capabilities.

providers.name: Ambarella
providers.description: Ambarella (NASDAQ: AMBA) is a fabless semiconductor company designing low-power system-on-chip (SoC) processors for edge AI and computer vision. Its CVflow architecture accelerates deep neural networks on-device for intelligent cameras, automotive ADAS and autonomous driving, robotics, security, and industrial applications. Ambarella does not publish a public HTTP/REST API; developers engage through the Cooper Developer Platform, the CVflow SDK and toolchain (compiler, debugger, Caffe/TensorFlow support), the Model Garden on HuggingFace, Agentic Blueprints, and an Apache-2.0 set of on-device Agent Skills for Cooper Foundry. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and enriched with the provider's real public developer, security, and agent surfaces.

providers.name: Group 1 Automotive
providers.description: Group 1 Automotive (NYSE: GPI) is an international Fortune 500 automotive retailer operating automotive dealerships, collision centers and service departments across the United States, the United Kingdom and Brazil, representing more than 35 vehicle brands. Group 1 does not operate a public developer program, but it does publish an AI-agent-facing surface: an llms.txt on www.group1auto.com and on its AcceleRide digital-retail site www.shopgroup1.com, each advertising a documented, parameterized, server-rendered vehicle-inventory browse endpoint at /llm/inventory/ that returns live new and used inventory (VIN, year, model, trim, mileage, price) without JavaScript, authentication, or an API key. There is no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP server, agent card, SDK or partner API reference published anywhere on the company's own hosts.

providers.name: Fueloyal
providers.description: Fueloyal is an automotive IoT and connected-vehicle platform company that builds proprietary IoT gateway hardware and software for fleet management, fuel management, predictive maintenance, dual dash cameras, EV services, and OEM connected-vehicle solutions. Its products help fleets and vehicle manufacturers monitor, connect, and service vehicles, with an OEM connected-platform and marketplace for delivering connected-vehicle services and mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Fueloyal was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Ridecell
providers.description: Ridecell is an AI-powered asset intelligence and orchestration platform for automotive leasing, fleet, and finance companies. Its five intelligence modules (Client, Spend, Supplier, Asset, and Operational Intelligence) and the "Maya" AI agent monitor fleets, flag invoice overcharges, track garage/supplier performance, optimize vehicle remarketing and residual value, and resolve idle-vehicle inefficiencies. The platform processes 12M+ events daily across 500K+ assets, 100+ connected systems, and 14+ countries. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Ridecell does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; this profile captures its public information, security, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Blackberry
providers.description: BlackBerry Limited is a Canadian intelligent security software and services company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, and listed on the NYSE and TSX as BB. Once known for its smartphones, BlackBerry today builds embedded and cybersecurity software for enterprises and governments. Its portfolio spans QNX (a real-time operating system for automotive and embedded/IoT systems), Cylance AI-driven endpoint protection, BlackBerry UEM (Unified Endpoint Management), BlackBerry AtHoc critical event management and mass notification, BlackBerry SecuSUITE secure voice and messaging, BlackBerry Workspaces secure file sharing, and the BlackBerry Dynamics secure mobility platform. Developers integrate with these products through REST APIs and SDKs, including the BlackBerry UEM Web Services REST API, the BlackBerry AtHoc API (v2, REST with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2 auth), and the BlackBerry Dynamics SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline from BlackBerry's public developer surface.

providers.name: Reynolds and Reynolds
providers.description: Reynolds and Reynolds is one of the automotive industry's largest Dealership Management System (DMS) providers, running the ERA-IGNITE and POWER platforms that operate the core of thousands of franchised car dealerships - sales and desking, F&I, service and repair orders, parts inventory, CRM, and dealership accounting. Reynolds does NOT publish an open, self-serve developer API. All programmatic access to DMS data flows through the Reynolds Certified Interface (RCI) program, a certification-gated, contract-and-NDA partner program run by Reynolds Data Management. RCI provides secured, real-time, bi-directional interfaces so certified third parties can read from and write back to a dealer's Reynolds DMS. There is no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no published OpenAPI. The APIs below are logical groupings of the DMS data domains exposed through RCI; endpoints are modeled, not sourced from public documentation.

providers.name: GirnarSoft
providers.description: GirnarSoft is an India-based enterprise software engineering and IT services company headquartered in Jaipur, Rajasthan, with a second delivery centre in Gurugram. Founded in 2007 by IIT Delhi alumni Amit and Anurag Jain, it is the technology arm of the CarDekho Group and built the consumer marketplaces CarDekho, BikeDekho, Gaadi, ZigWheels and PriceDekho. The firm sells outsourced product engineering rather than a product API: staff augmentation, dedicated teams and software outsourcing across web and mobile development, QA and test automation, business intelligence, data science, AI/ML, cloud and DevOps, plus AI-augmented engineering pods and agentic-AI automation. It works in banking, insurance, automotive, retail and e-commerce, edtech, SaaS, travel and government/PSU, and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: Amkor Technology
providers.description: Amkor Technology is the world's largest US-based provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services (OSAT), serving integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor companies, and contract foundries. The company offers advanced packaging technologies including flip chip, wafer-level packaging, 2.5D/3D TSV, System-in-Package, and chiplet integration solutions for AI, automotive, communications, computing, consumer electronics, industrial, IoT, and networking markets.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Root Insurance
providers.description: Root is a U.S. app-first auto insurer that prices policies primarily on real driving behavior captured by smartphone telematics. The Root mobile app handles enrollment, telematics scoring, policy management, claims, and optional roadside assistance, with renters insurance as an add-on line. Root has reorganized its tech stack around APIs to power embedded auto insurance with partners such as Carvana and Hyundai Capital America; partner APIs are gated and not publicly documented. Note: Root Insurance (joinroot.com) is distinct from the unrelated Root Platform (rootplatform.com) insurtech in South Africa / UK.

providers.name: ACV
providers.description: ACV Auctions (NASDAQ: ACVA) operates the nation's largest online wholesale marketplace and daily auto auction platform, connecting franchise and independent dealers to buy and sell used vehicles. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Buffalo, New York, ACV pairs a mobile-first bidding app with third-party vehicle inspections and condition reports, real-time market data (ACV MAX and market insights), transportation logistics, and dealer floor-plan financing through ACV Capital. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; ACV does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Schaeffler
providers.description: Schaeffler Group is a German global Tier 1 automotive and industrial supplier headquartered in Herzogenaurach. Schaeffler designs and manufactures precision bearings, powertrain components, chassis applications, and e-mobility systems for the automotive and industrial sectors.

providers.name: Valeo
providers.description: Valeo is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Paris. Valeo designs and manufactures comfort and driving assistance, powertrain, thermal, and visibility systems for the automotive industry, with a strong focus on electrification and ADAS.

providers.name: Click Mechanic
providers.description: ClickMechanic is the UK's leading online car-repair marketplace, founded in 2012, that connects car owners with vetted mobile mechanics and independent garages for repairs, servicing, diagnostics, and MOTs. Customers enter their registration and symptoms to get an instant fixed-price quote, then book a vetted mechanic for same- or next-day work at home or the roadside, with payment taken only after the job is completed. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. ClickMechanic operates a consumer- and mechanic-facing web platform (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API catalog at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aisin
providers.description: Aisin Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Kariya, Aichi. Part of the Toyota Group, Aisin manufactures automatic transmissions, drivetrain components, body, chassis, and electronics for major automakers.

providers.name: Hutchinson
providers.description: Hutchinson SA is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Paris, a subsidiary of TotalEnergies. Hutchinson designs and manufactures anti-vibration systems, sealing systems, fluid transfer, precision rubber components, and aerospace systems for the automotive, aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors.

providers.name: iMotorbike
providers.description: iMotorbike is a Southeast Asian online marketplace and service platform for buying, selling, and servicing pre-owned motorcycles, operating across Malaysia and Vietnam. Sellers submit their bike details, book a free inspection, receive a quotation, and get paid fast, while iMotorbike handles loan settlement and JPJ ownership transfer on their behalf. Buyers shop iM Certified motorcycles backed by a 170-point inspection, a 12-month warranty, and a 6-day return policy, and can book test rides, inspections, and roadside assistance (iM Rescue) through the platform. Founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global, Headline, Gobi Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst, iMotorbike closed a US$10M Series A in 2025 to expand across the region. The company runs a consumer-facing web marketplace and an internal admin platform; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Speero
providers.description: Speero (سبيرو) is Saudi Arabia's online marketplace for authentic automotive spare parts, accessories, and professional vehicle services. The platform helps car owners find OEM and aftermarket parts for their specific make and model across all major categories (engine, brakes, suspension, lighting, AC, exhaust, and more) and book maintenance, detailing, paint and dent repair, tinting, and tire care at trusted workshops across the Kingdom. It supports browse-by-vehicle, installment payment options, and WhatsApp-based customer support. Speero is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer marketplace and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose a machine-discovery surface (llms.txt, RFC 9116 security.txt, and an RFC 9727 api-catalog linkset).

providers.name: Xtime
providers.description: Xtime is Cox Automotive's service experience platform for franchised auto dealerships, combining online appointment scheduling, service-lane check-in, multi-point vehicle inspection, customer communications, service marketing, and payments into one fixed-operations workflow. Part of Cox Automotive since 2014 alongside Dealertrack, VinSolutions, Kelley Blue Book, and vAuto, Xtime integrates with DMS and dealer-website partners through the Cox Automotive ecosystem; it publishes no public self-serve API or developer portal, with partner integration handled via the Cox Automotive Integration Platform.

providers.name: Continental AG
providers.description: Continental AG is a German multinational automotive supplier and tire manufacturer headquartered in Hanover. As a global Tier 1 automotive supplier, Continental designs and manufactures tires, automotive electronics, brake systems, powertrain components, ADAS, and interior solutions for vehicle manufacturers worldwide.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: Backlotcars
providers.description: BacklotCars, Inc. is a dealer-to-dealer wholesale used-vehicle marketplace, founded in Kansas City and acquired by KAR Global (now OPENLANE, Inc.), whose technology was consolidated into the OPENLANE US marketplace. It connects thousands of franchise and independent dealers through a 24/7 bid-ask marketplace, "Buy It Now" listings, and timed auctions scheduled throughout each week, backed by native mobile apps, in-lane vehicle inspections with AI-analyzed engine recordings, transportation, and floor-plan financing. Commercial sellers and dealer groups can push inventory straight from their own systems into OPENLANE Sell via OPENLANE Connect, a lightweight dealer integration API with a dedicated test environment. This profile began as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network and was enriched from OPENLANE's public marketing and product surface; the platform publishes no public OpenAPI or open developer portal.

providers.name: Spiffy
providers.description: Get Spiffy, Inc. (Spiffy) is a B2B SaaS and operations company that sells a mobile service operating system to franchise car dealerships. Its core product, Mobile 360, is an enterprise platform covering scheduling, dispatch, route optimization, technician management, digital vehicle inspections, DMS integration and customer communication, sold as a turnkey program alongside van upfits, connected devices (Easy Tread, Easy Flow, Smart Tumbler) and technician training. Spiffy also runs fleet and Amazon DSP service programs, and operates a customer booking portal and a fleet portal. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Apex, North Carolina, the company has raised more than $90M and reports over 4 million completed services, with OEM work including a Hyundai Motor America pilot. Spiffy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; its Fleet portal API is an internal, credentialed surface with no published contract.

providers.name: Avatr Technology
providers.description: AVATR Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. (阿维塔科技) is a Chinese premium intelligent electric-vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Chongqing, founded in 2018 as a joint venture in which Changan Automobile and CATL are the two largest shareholders and Huawei supplies the smart-cockpit and advanced driver-assistance stack. Its vehicles — the AVATR 11 and 12, the volume 06 and 07 (battery-electric and range-extended), and the limited 011 and 012 — are built on the jointly developed CHN smart-EV platform, a six-layer architecture spanning the mechanical, energy, electronic/electrical architecture, vehicle operating system, vehicle function application and cloud big-data layers. AVATR produced 73,606 vehicles in 2024 and sells through mainland China plus overseas markets including Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Qatar, with design and engineering offices in Shanghai and Munich. AVATR is a vehicle manufacturer, not a software vendor: www.avatr.com is a marketing and configurator site with no developer portal, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification. The only live agent surface anywhere on an AVATR hostname is platform-provided — the official Hong Kong site runs on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint plus a Wix-generated llms.txt over its public marketing content.

providers.name: Denso
providers.description: Denso Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive components manufacturer headquartered in Kariya, Aichi. Denso designs and supplies thermal, powertrain, mobility electronics, and electrification systems to global automakers.

providers.name: Forvia
providers.description: Forvia is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier formed in 2022 by the combination of Faurecia and Hella. Forvia designs and manufactures cockpits, seating, interiors, lighting, electronics, hydrogen storage, and clean mobility systems for global automakers.

providers.name: Gestamp
providers.description: Gestamp Automocion is a Spanish global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Madrid. Gestamp designs and manufactures metal components for vehicle bodies, chassis, and mechanisms, with focus on lightweighting and structural safety for global automakers.

providers.name: Hyundai Mobis
providers.description: Hyundai Mobis is a South Korean global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Seoul. Part of the Hyundai Motor Group, Mobis designs and manufactures chassis, cockpit, and front-end modules, plus electrification, ADAS, and infotainment systems for global automakers.

providers.name: Magna International
providers.description: Magna International is a Canadian global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Aurora, Ontario. Magna designs and manufactures vehicle bodies, chassis, exteriors, seating, powertrain, ADAS, electronics, mirrors, and complete vehicle assembly through its global operations.

providers.name: MAHLE
providers.description: MAHLE is a German global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Stuttgart. MAHLE designs and manufactures thermal management, electrification, engine systems and components, filtration, and mechatronics for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and off-highway equipment.

providers.name: Yazaki
providers.description: Yazaki Corporation is a Japanese global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Tokyo. Yazaki is a leading manufacturer of automotive wiring harnesses, connectors, instrumentation, and electrical distribution systems for global automakers.

providers.name: ZF Friedrichshafen
providers.description: ZF Friedrichshafen AG is a German global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Friedrichshafen. ZF designs and manufactures driveline, chassis, active and passive safety, and ADAS technology for passenger cars and commercial vehicles. ZF acquired TRW Automotive in 2015.

providers.name: Lemonaide
providers.description: Lemonaide is a Bangkok-headquartered B2B used-car and insurtech platform operating across Southeast Asia, positioning itself as a technology and services layer that reduces asymmetric information in the automotive market. The company sells software to used-car dealerships and insurers, including a Dealer Management System, a Dealer CRM with microtargeting, and a Digital Escrow settlement product, alongside operated services such as after-sales BPO, warranty third-party administration, 24-hour digital roadside assistance, vehicle inspection, and repair-workshop audit assessment. Lemonaide states that more than 2,000 dealers use its platform and names Carro, Carsome, and Toyota Sure among its partners. It is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Lemonaide publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Bosch
providers.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

providers.name: CarNow
providers.description: CarNow is an AI-enabled conversion platform built specifically for automotive dealerships, helping them turn more website visitors into leads, more leads into sales, and more buyers into lifelong service customers. Its product suite spans website solutions (AI-powered chat, digital retail, and shop-by-payment experiences), sales follow-up automation (Cruise Control, which prioritizes high-intent shoppers and automates nurture workflows), and service retention (Lane Assist, which drives post-sale engagement and service scheduling). CarNow works with more than 4,000 dealer partners and integrates with major OEM programs including Acura, Audi, BMW, Ford, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Land Rover, and Lexus. The company is headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina and is backed by Battery Ventures. CarNow does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs; its api.carnow.com endpoint is a partner/internal AWS API Gateway that requires authentication.

providers.name: Gamma Technologies
providers.description: Gamma Technologies develops GT-SUITE, the multi-physics system simulation software used by engineers to model, simulate, and optimize complex systems across automotive, HVACR, aerospace, industrial machinery, and shipbuilding. GT-SUITE combines 0D/1D/3D physics-based modeling, prebuilt model libraries, digital-twin workflows, and native AI tooling (GT Intelligence Studio and a Machine Learning Assistant). The company is a desktop/engineering CAE vendor rather than an API-first provider and publishes no public REST API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.

providers.name: Hyundai
providers.description: Hyundai Motor Company is a South Korean multinational automotive manufacturer specializing in designing and producing a wide range of vehicles including cars, SUVs, and commercial vehicles. Hyundai operates a developer portal exposing connected vehicle services, mobility solutions, and partner integration touchpoints.

providers.name: Slate Auto
providers.description: Slate Auto is an American electric-vehicle manufacturer building a radically simple, affordable, and customizable electric pickup truck. Designed in California and Michigan, engineered in Michigan, and assembled in the Midwest, the "Blank Slate" starts around $24,950 and offers roughly 205 miles of range, with interchangeable body panels and 200+ accessories that let owners reconfigure the vehicle over its life (including SUV and Fastback body styles). Slate sells direct through a preorder/reservation model, rejects mandatory feature packages and large touchscreens in favor of durability and owner control, and offers fleet solutions. Backed by General Catalyst. As a consumer automaker, Slate Auto publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Insurify
providers.description: Insurify is an insurance comparison marketplace licensed in all 50 U.S. states with real-time API integrations into 120+ carriers (500+ across the carrier network), covering auto, home, renters, pet, commercial auto, life, motorcycle, and travel. Consumers get side-by-side quotes in roughly two minutes and can buy online or through licensed agents. Insurify's Evia AI agent (Expert Virtual Insurance Agent) is a voice-and-chat agent that handles end-to-end shopping conversations with bind-ready quotes and renewal-cycle re-shopping. In February 2026 Insurify launched the insurance industry's first ChatGPT app via OpenAI's app library.

providers.name: vAuto
providers.description: vAuto is a Cox Automotive brand providing new and used vehicle inventory management, appraisal, pricing, and merchandising software for automotive dealers (ProfitTime GPS, Provision, Conquest, Stockwave). vAuto exposes partner-gated APIs through the Cox Automotive Integration Platform (developer.coxautoinc.com) - notably the vAuto Inventory API and the vAuto Appraisal API - that let authorized integrators programmatically read vehicle inventory, update list price, and create and access appraisals in the vAuto ecosystem. Access is not open self-service; integrators must be approved partners, authenticate via Cox Automotive Bridge ID / OAuth with an issued API key, and endpoint-level reference documentation is behind the partner developer portal login. Per-path endpoints below are modeled from the published product summaries, not copied from public reference docs.

providers.name: Acerta
providers.description: Acerta (Acerta Analytics Solutions Inc.) is a Canadian industrial-AI company whose LinePulse platform delivers AI-driven manufacturing quality analytics for discrete manufacturing. Founded in 2017 in Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Acerta helps Tier-1 automotive and powertrain manufacturers detect defects early, reduce scrap and rework, and root-cause complex production issues in real time. LinePulse replaces statistical process control software, spreadsheets, and custom querying tools with real-time SPC, predictive monitoring, and machine-learning root-cause analysis, and ingests production data through a proprietary secure ingestion API. The platform is built on Microsoft Azure, is SOC 2 Type 1 certified, and is proven across 300+ production lines in 12 countries with customers including BorgWarner, Dana, Linamar, Ford, ZF, Ballard, and BMW. Acerta is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. Acerta exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, self-serve sign-up, or SDKs; integration is delivered through enterprise deployment with the LinePulse ingestion API.

providers.name: Asbury Automotive Group
providers.description: Asbury Automotive Group is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, operating new and used vehicle dealerships across multiple states and brands. Headquartered in Duluth, Georgia, Asbury operates approximately 200 dealerships representing 30+ automotive brands including luxury and non-luxury vehicles. The company operates under multiple brand names including Coggin Automotive Group, Crown Automotive Group, Park Place Dealerships, Nalley Automotive Group, and others. Asbury does not expose a public developer API but operates digital retail platforms including Clicklane, their proprietary online vehicle purchase platform.

providers.name: Dana Incorporated
providers.description: Dana Incorporated is a global supplier of fully integrated drivetrain and electrified propulsion systems for passenger, commercial, and off-highway vehicles. Dana announced an agreement in 2025 for its Off-Highway business to be acquired by Allison Transmission. Dana's main public API surface is the Dana Aftermarket developer platform; this repository is an alias of the primary "dana" profile.

providers.name: Green Hills Software
providers.description: Green Hills Software is a privately held embedded software company founded in 1982 by Dan O'Dowd and Carl Rosenberg and headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. It builds safety- and security-certified real-time operating systems (INTEGRITY, INTEGRITY-178 tuMP, u-velOSity), embedded hypervisors (INTEGRITY Multivisor, u-visor), optimizing C/C++/Ada/Fortran compilers, the MULTI and AdaMULTI integrated development environments, the TimeMachine back-in-time debug suite, the DoubleCheck static analyzer, the Green Hills Probe hardware debugger, and networking, file-system and USB middleware. Its customers ship these components inside aerospace, defense, automotive, medical, industrial, rail, telecommunications and consumer devices. Green Hills is a toolchain and operating-system vendor rather than an API provider: the programmable interfaces it ships are in-product C/C++, POSIX and MULTI-Python scripting APIs delivered with a licensed installation and documented in manuals distributed with the product, and its technical support portal at support.ghs.com requires an account. No public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API description was found on any Green Hills host during enrichment.

providers.name: HAAS Alert
providers.description: HAAS Alert operates Safety Cloud, a connected-vehicle safety platform that delivers real-time digital alerts to nearby motorists about active emergency responses, roadside hazards, work zones, stopped vehicles, and slow-moving equipment. Using vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and cellular messaging, Safety Cloud gives drivers up to roughly 30 seconds of advance warning to help reduce collisions with first responders, tow operators, and roadway workers. HAAS Alert integrates with telematics platforms, fleet manufacturers, OEM vehicles, in-car navigation (including Waze), and roadway infrastructure to form a large connected-vehicle alerting ecosystem. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from HAAS Alert's public web surface; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs were found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Adient
providers.description: Adient is a global automotive seating supplier headquartered in Plymouth, Michigan. Spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016, Adient designs and manufactures seating systems for global automakers across passenger and commercial vehicles.

providers.name: BizzyCar
providers.description: BizzyCar is a B2B SaaS platform for automotive dealerships that automates service recall management, customer outreach and mobile service. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Saint Peters, Missouri, the company ingests VIN-level open-recall data from OEM partners, matches it against a dealer's market area and DMS records, then uses AI-driven outreach (SMS, email, voice) to book service appointments and dispatch mobile service vans. Products include Recall Outreach, Recall Scout, Recall Radar, Service Engine, Mobile Service and Fleet IQ. BizzyCar is primarily an API *consumer* rather than an API producer: it ships pre-built connectors into dealer management systems (Dealertrack, DMS Plus, Open/Mate, Asbury, PBS, Tekion, Fortellis, Reynolds & Reynolds) and service schedulers (Xtime, TCC, DealerFX, Affinitiv, Update Promise), but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract of its own.

providers.name: Cars24
providers.description: Cars24 (CARS24 Services Private Limited) is one of India's largest auto-tech companies and an online marketplace for buying and selling used cars, operating across India, the UAE, and Australia. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana, Cars24 is an RBI-registered NBFC that combines a used-car transaction platform with financing, insurance, and vehicle-management services. Its offerings include buying and selling pre-owned cars with 300+ point inspections, fixed transparent pricing, warranties, and doorstep delivery; AI-driven used-car valuation; new-car discovery; traffic challan checking and payment; pre-delivery inspections across 220+ cities; vehicle history and service-history reports; car scrapping; FASTag recharge; and used-car loans, loan-against-car, and personal-loan products through Bikes24, Insure24, and related brands. Cars24 is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and 500 Global. It is a consumer platform and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, agent-facing llms.txt, and security posture.

providers.name: Invygo
providers.description: Invygo is a car subscription and flexible rental platform founded in 2018 in Dubai, offering an alternative to traditional car ownership across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers subscribe to a car on a weekly or monthly basis, or enroll in a 36-month, Sharia-compliant "Subscribe to Own" plan, with insurance, maintenance, registration, and roadside assistance bundled into an all-inclusive fee and no deposit, salary certificate, or bank loan required. Invygo reports 20,000+ active subscriptions across 15+ cities in the GCC. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its public web, legal, and security surface.

providers.name: ams OSRAM
providers.description: ams OSRAM (ams-OSRAM AG) is a global leader in innovative optical solutions, designing and manufacturing intelligent sensors, emitters, and light-based semiconductors. Formed from the 2020 combination of ams AG (Austria) and OSRAM (Germany), the company builds LEDs, VCSEL and edge-emitting lasers, CMOS image sensors, ambient light and proximity sensors, direct time-of-flight (dToF) sensors, photodiodes, and LED/VCSEL driver ICs. Its sensing, illumination, and visualization technologies serve automotive and mobility (headlamps, interior lighting, ADAS), industrial automation and robotics, medical and healthcare devices, mobile and wearable devices, computing, and general lighting. Headquartered in Premstaetten, Austria and Munich, Germany, ams OSRAM employs roughly 18,500 people across 25 R&D sites and holds over 12,000 patents. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of iconiq-capital and enriched from ams OSRAM public web pages; the company exposes product/design support and a download center rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Bridgestone
providers.description: Bridgestone Corporation is a Japanese global tire and rubber manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo. Bridgestone produces tires for passenger, commercial, off-road, and aircraft applications, plus diversified rubber and chemical products, and is one of the largest tire makers in the world.

providers.name: Helm.ai
providers.description: Helm.ai is an AI software company for autonomous driving and robotics, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. It develops camera-first perception, path prediction and end-to-end autonomy stacks — Helm.ai Vision and Helm.ai Driver — alongside the generative AI development and validation tools VidGen-3, GenSim-3 and WorldGen-1, all trained with its proprietary Deep Teaching unsupervised learning method. The software is licensed to automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers (Honda, Volkswagen, Ambarella, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Texas Instruments) as embedded, hardware-agnostic components for production vehicle programs rather than as a public developer API. As of 2026-08-22 the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification on any host it controls.

providers.name: Invisible AI
providers.description: Invisible AI is a next-generation computer vision company delivering a Vision Execution System (VES) for manufacturing. NVIDIA Jetson-powered edge devices with Intel RealSense 3D depth cameras and on-device SSD storage mount to existing factory infrastructure and, within hours, encode and segment the production floor in real time. The no-code, edge-based platform captures 100% of production cycles across every station without wearables, operator disruption, or cloud integration, then analyzes human motion and objects to surface cycle-time variability, process drift, quality escapes, and safety/ergonomics risk. Founded in 2018 by autonomous-vehicle veterans and backed by Sierra Ventures, it serves automotive and aerospace OEMs including Toyota, Ford, General Motors, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Nissan. Invisible AI publishes no public API or developer platform today; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PlotAPI
providers.description: Automotive and property data API. The published surface covers US VIN histories and vehicle specifications, UK MOT records, auto parts fitment catalogues, vehicle valuations, and property listings for the UK and US markets, served as typed JSON over a single REST endpoint. Positioned for AI agents and for developers who would otherwise integrate several gated data sources separately. The product is real and live; what is not public is the interface — documentation, the API reference and key issuance all sit behind an account sign-in, and the machine-readable artifacts the site advertises are not currently served.

providers.name: ACV Auctions
providers.description: ACV Auctions is a digital wholesale marketplace for the automotive industry, operating the leading online platform for dealer-to-dealer used-vehicle auctions across the United States. Franchise and independent dealers source and sell inventory through daily online auctions backed by third-party vehicle inspections, detailed condition reports, and the company's data and analytics products. ACV also offers complementary services including vehicle transportation, dealer floor-plan financing through ACV Capital, and inventory-management and pricing tools. The company is publicly traded and headquartered in Buffalo, New York. It does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Carma
providers.description: Carma is an Australian online used-car retailer that lets consumers buy, sell, and trade in pre-owned vehicles entirely online. Every car is inspected and reconditioned, and the platform bundles financing through partner lenders, home delivery, trade-in valuations, a 7-day money-back guarantee, a 3-month warranty, and NRMA roadside assistance as an alternative to the traditional dealership experience. Backed by General Catalyst since 2022, Carma is headquartered in Sydney, Australia. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched from Carma's public web surface; Carma publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Nissan
providers.description: Nissan is a multinational automaker that designs, manufactures, and sells a wide range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and SUVs. They are known for their innovative technology and commitment to sustainability, with a focus on producing electric and hybrid vehicles. In addition to their automotive business, Nissan also invests in research and development to create new products and services that cater to the changing needs of consumers.

providers.name: Rimac Automobili
providers.description: Rimac Automobili d.o.o. is a Croatian electric hypercar manufacturer and automotive technology company founded by Mate Rimac in 2009 and headquartered at the Rimac Campus in Kerestinec, near Zagreb. It designs and builds the Nevera and Nevera R all-electric hypercars, and develops the vehicle software, infotainment, connectivity and telemetry stack that runs them in-house. Since the 2021 formation of the Bugatti Rimac joint venture with Porsche, the group's component and OEM-supply business was carved out into the sister company Rimac Technology, while Rimac Automobili remains the vehicle brand. Rimac operates a private, customer-only connected-vehicle backend — an MQTT-based telemetry platform feeding first-party iOS and Android owner apps with location, charging, battery and driving-performance data, plus over-the-air update and remote command channels — but it publishes no public developer program, developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio tracking.

providers.name: American Axle and Manufacturing
providers.description: American Axle & Manufacturing (AAM), now operating as Dauch Corporation following the February 2026 acquisition of Dowlais Group (GKN Automotive and GKN Powder Metallurgy), is a global Tier 1 automotive supplier designing, engineering, and manufacturing driveline and metal forming technologies for electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. AAM operates an iSupplier Portal for supplier communication, EDI integration for forecasts and releases, and the Demand AAM aftermarket parts portal.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: Brumbrum
providers.description: Brumbrum is an Italian online used-car marketplace, part of the pan-European Aramis Group, that sells certified pre-owned vehicles fully online with home delivery, financing, trade-in (permuta), warranty coverage, a 14-day return trial and a best-price guarantee. Vehicles are inspected and reconditioned at its Reggio Emilia facility (300+ quality checks) with retail presence near Milan. Brumbrum is a consumer e-commerce brand rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification. This profile in the API Evangelist network captures the company's public web identity and the security/discovery signals probed from its domain.

providers.name: Finn
providers.description: FINN (finn.com) is a Munich-based consumer car-subscription service that lets individuals and businesses lease a car on a flexible monthly subscription, with insurance, maintenance, registration, taxes, and roadside assistance bundled into one all-inclusive price. Subscribers pick from more than twenty vehicle brands on terms from six to twenty-four months, and the company also runs a fleet/business offering. Backed by HV Capital, FINN operates in Germany, the United States, and other European markets. FINN is a consumer, direct-to-customer business with no public developer API or partner API program surfaced at this time; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flease
providers.description: Flease is a French vehicle-leasing marketplace offering flexible long-term (LLD, 24-50 month) and medium-term (LMD, 1-12 month) car and utility-vehicle rental to SMEs and small businesses. It sources quasi-new vehicles (under two years old, fewer than 30,000 km), delivers within a week for LMD and a month for LLD, and bundles a fleet-management web application (webapp.flease.fr) for tracking mileage, drivers, maintenance, contracts, and invoices. Flease positions on transparent pricing and a roughly 20% lower total cost of ownership versus traditional leasing, with a circular-economy angle of redeploying used vehicles. Backed by Partech. No public developer API or documentation is published; the customer-facing webapp is a Vue single-page app authenticated with AWS Cognito.

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: AutoZone
providers.description: AutoZone is the nation's leading retailer and a leading distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories with more than 7,000 stores across the Americas. AutoZone serves both do-it-yourself (DIY) customers and professional automotive service providers (DIFM) through retail stores, e-commerce, and electronic ordering integrations for commercial accounts via AutoZone Pro.

providers.name: Clickable
providers.description: Clickable is a marketing analytics and digital advertising platform founded in 2006 that serves as an ads and analytics partner for businesses and agencies. The company builds award-winning pay-per-click (PPC) advertising tools for search and social campaigns and delivers customized reporting that cuts through data overload so marketers can focus on the metrics that matter. Clickable also offers VIN retention reporting purpose-built for automotive dealerships to improve customer retention. Backed by Union Square Ventures, the company focuses on relationship-driven managed advertising and analytics services rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Certivity
providers.description: Certivity is a Munich-based RegTech company, founded in 2021, that operates an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform for regulated industries such as automotive, aerospace, and connected vehicles. Its product, Certivity Core, turns complex regulations, standards, and internal documents into structured, machine-readable, engineering-ready requirements with full traceability and real-time monitoring of legal changes across 50+ jurisdictions. The platform digitizes and structures regulatory content from publishers such as ISO, IEC, CEN, CENELEC, ASTM, UL, and SAE using a proprietary ingestion pipeline and a regulatory knowledge graph, and integrates directly into engineering workflows (including Jama Connect) via an official API. Backed by Earlybird, High-Tech Gruenderfonds, UVC Partners, and Almaz Capital, Certivity added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Edge Case Research
providers.description: Edge Case Research (operating as "Edge Case", ecr.ai) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania company founded in 2013 that provides functional safety engineering, risk management and safety-assurance software for autonomous and other "frontier technology" systems. Its DevSafeOps methodology carries safety through the whole product lifecycle — hazard identification in design, verified safety evidence in build, and continuous safety monitoring in operations — and its nLoop live-safety-case platform assembles evidence from design, simulation, test and field operations into an auditable, continuously updated safety case. The company works across aerospace and defense, automotive and autonomous trucking, space, oil and gas, and supply chain and logistics, and publishes the Open Autonomy Safety Case framework as SACM XML on GitHub. Edge Case publishes no public product API or OpenAPI; the only machine-readable surface reachable on its own host is the Wix-provided site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Modern Meadow
providers.description: Modern Meadow is a bio-design and materials-science company founded in 2011 in Brooklyn by Andras Forgacs, Francoise Marga, Gabor Forgacs and Karoly Jakab, now headquartered in Nutley / Pine Brook, New Jersey, where it operates an innovation lab opened in 2017. The company applies synthetic biology and protein engineering to build animal-free, bio-fabricated alternatives to leather and other petrochemical-derived materials, through the Bio-Alloy technology platform (an alloy of engineered proteins and bio-based polymers), the BIO-VERA material launched in 2023, and its current flagship INNOVERA, a next-generation leather alternative made from plant proteins, biopolymers and recycled rubber with more than 80% renewable carbon content. It sells into interiors, fashion and accessories, footwear, and automotive, and has partnered with BASF, tannery HELLER-LEDER (a 2026 European joint venture) and Allbirds (the Terralux footwear line). Modern Meadow has raised roughly $236M. It is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: profiling on 2026-08-01 found no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no /.well-known/ documents, and no GitHub organization. Its corporate site (modernmeadow.com, Craft CMS) largely redirects to the product site innovera-world.com.

providers.name: Spinny
providers.description: Spinny (Valuedrive Technologies Ltd.) is an India-based online marketplace for buying and selling used cars. Every Spinny Assured car undergoes a 200-point quality check and comes with a 1-year warranty, a 5-day money-back guarantee, and hassle-free RC ownership transfer. The platform also offers instant online car valuation, doorstep evaluation, used-car finance and EMI, car insurance, RC transfer, scrap-car service, e-Challan and RTO lookups, servicing, the Spinny Max luxury tier, and a Partners auction platform for dealers. Backed by Accel and General Catalyst. Spinny publishes a consumer web experience and an llms.txt for AI agents but does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Vay
providers.description: Vay is a Berlin-headquartered teledriving (remote driving) mobility company, founded in 2018 by Thomas von der Ohe, Fabrizio Scelsi, and Bogdan Djukic, that operates the first commercial remotely driven car service. Customers in Las Vegas rent cars by the minute that are delivered and parked driverless by professional remote drivers from a Remote Driving Center; the company runs a 175-vehicle fleet, has served 50,000+ trips, and raised a Series C from Grab in December 2025. Vay is a consumer mobility service and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: MayMaan Research
providers.description: MayMaan Research is a clean-energy engineering company that redesigns the internal combustion engine around its patented AquaStroke platform, a piston engine that runs on a blend of roughly 70% water and 30% bio-alcohol (ethanol or methanol) instead of gasoline or diesel. The company builds modular generator sets and powertrains that scale from a 35 kW unit (A35) through the AV2 to multi-megawatt installations, and it positions them as drop-in replacements for diesel gensets in power generation, EV charging infrastructure, data centers, telecommunications, marine, construction, agriculture, defense and off-grid deployments, with near-zero NOx, SOx, CO2 and particulate output. MayMaan is headquartered in Hollywood, Florida with a European office in Paris, holds engine and fuel-system patents internationally, and raised a $30 million Series A led by WAVE Equity Partners. It is a hardware manufacturer: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: StoreDot
providers.description: StoreDot is an Israeli battery technology company founded in 2012 by Doron Myersdorf, Simon Litsyn and Gil Rosenman, headquartered in Herzliya with an advanced technology campus in Irvine, California. It develops extreme fast charging (XFC) lithium-ion cells built on proprietary silicon-dominant anode chemistry and synthesized organic and inorganic compounds optimized with machine-learning models, targeting the range and charging anxiety that gate mainstream electric-vehicle adoption. Its "100inX" product roadmap sets 100 miles of range charged in 5 minutes (100in5, 2024), 3 minutes (100in3, 2028) and 2 minutes (100in2, 2032); the company has demonstrated pouch and prismatic XFC cells sustaining more than 1,000 and later 2,000 extreme fast charging cycles while retaining over 80 percent of original capacity, and designs its chemistry to drop into existing Li-ion production lines. Strategic investors and partners include Daimler/Mercedes-Benz, BP, VinFast, Volvo, Polestar, Ola Electric, Samsung Ventures, TDK and manufacturing partner EVE Energy. In 2026 a planned SPAC merger with Andretti Acquisition Corp. II was terminated and the company returned to private fundraising. StoreDot is a hardware, materials and cell-manufacturing business: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server or machine-readable API contract, and no /.well-known/ discovery surface, llms.txt or developer subdomain resolves on store-dot.com.

providers.name: actnano
providers.description: actnano, Inc. is a Massachusetts-based advanced materials company that develops and manufactures PFAS-free protective nanocoatings for electronics. Its flagship Advanced nanoGUARD technology is a gel-state, 100% fluorine-free conformal coating applied to printed circuit board assemblies, connectors, antennas, LEDs and high-heat-generating components, delivering up to IPx8 moisture and condensation protection without trapping heat or degrading signal integrity. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with a Munich center of excellence and operations in Mexico and Japan, actnano serves mobility and automotive electronics, consumer electronics, AI and data-center infrastructure, solar, industrial electronics, medical devices and optical anti-fog applications. The company states REACH and RoHS compliance and ISO 9001:2015 certification, and is backed by BMW i Ventures, Porsche Ventures and Emerald Technology Ventures. actnano is a materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Catena-X
providers.description: Catena-X is the automotive industry's data space standard, published by Catena-X Automotive Network e.V. — a non-commercial German registered association founded on 15 May 2021 by BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, Bosch, SAP, Siemens, Schaeffler, ZF, BASF, Henkel, Deutsche Telekom and Fraunhofer, with backing from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action. It publishes a numbered CX-xxxx library of 77 standards covering how a supply chain exchanges part data, carbon footprints, quality records, demand and capacity signals and digital product passports without any participant surrendering its data to a central platform.
