Standards move forward together in named releases — Jupiter, Io, Saturn, Titan — gated by a Technical Committee for Standardization, and conformance is certified by nominated third-party assessment bodies including TÜV Rheinland and TÜV SÜD. The reference implementation is open source as Eclipse Tractus-X, and the network is operated commercially by Cofinity-X. It is the most institutionally complete industry API standard in Europe, and the one whose endpoints an outside developer can never call: in a data space every participant runs its own connector and registry, so there is nothing to call until you are onboarded, credentialed and certified.

providers.name: Internet Brands
providers.description: Internet Brands is a KKR-owned digital media and software company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that operates a portfolio of vertical franchises across health, dental, legal, and auto/home/travel markets. Its brands include WebMD and Medscape (health), WebMD Ignite and PulsePoint (health engagement), Henry Schein One and Dentrix (dental SaaS), FindLaw and Avvo (legal), and CarsDirect and Fodor's (auto, home, and travel). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The holding company does not publish a single unified public developer API; developer surfaces live with its individual operating brands.

providers.name: Modine Manufacturing
providers.description: Modine Manufacturing is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Modine Manufacturing API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Carwow
providers.description: Carwow is a UK-based online automotive marketplace that helps consumers buy, sell, lease, and finance cars without haggling or hidden fees. Buyers browse new and used car deals, compare dealer quotes, arrange leasing (including salary sacrifice and fleet through Carwow Leasey), find electric-vehicle deals, and access vehicle financing and credit brokering. Sellers get free car valuations, part-exchange, and van sales. Carwow also publishes professional car reviews and ratings, runs a large YouTube channel, and offers comparison tools, EV charging maps, a car history checker, and insurance services. Founded in London and backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Carwow operates across the UK and Europe. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source engineering tooling but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Sonatus
providers.description: Sonatus, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California automotive software company, founded in 2018, that builds cloud-to-edge vehicle AI software for software-defined vehicles (SDVs). Its Fastlane platform pairs in-vehicle Fastlane Edge software with Fastlane Collector for dynamic, policy-driven vehicle data collection, Fastlane Insight for cloud-side analysis, and Fastlane Copilot for quick-start integration, alongside the Sonatus Automator vehicle-automation product. Sonatus states its technology is deployed in more than eight million vehicles worldwide, and it is backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Kia, LG, Marvell, NEC, Foxconn and Translink Capital. Sonatus sells to vehicle OEMs and tier-one suppliers rather than to individual developers: it markets an SDK comprising Sonatus Automator, APIs and documentation, but that developer surface is delivered to contracted OEM customers and is not published on any public developer portal.

providers.name: TrueCar
providers.description: TrueCar is a Santa Monica, California based online automotive marketplace that connects car buyers with a nationwide network of certified dealers, publishing upfront, transparent pricing on new and used vehicles alongside what other buyers in the same area actually paid. The company operates truecar.com, the TrueCar+ end-to-end digital retail experience, a sell-your-car / instant cash offer service, and white-label car-buying programs for affinity partners such as credit unions, insurers and large employers. Founded in 2005 by Scott Painter, TrueCar traded on NASDAQ as TRUE until January 2026, when Fair Holdings, Inc. - led by Painter, with PenFed Credit Union, Zurich North America, AutoNation and Atlantic Coast Automotive - completed a $227 million take-private acquisition. TrueCar publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract; its dealer, DMS and OEM integrations are arranged privately through the dealer portal under commercial agreement.

providers.name: Virtuo
providers.description: Virtuo (govirtuo.com) is a Paris-based, next-generation car rental company founded in 2015 and backed by Balderton Capital. It replaces the traditional rental counter with a mobile app: customers book, unlock, and return premium connected vehicles (Mercedes, BMW, Audi, Peugeot, Renault, Toyota, Volkswagen and others) entirely from their phone, with delivery options, free cancellation, and 24/7 support across 100+ locations in Europe. Virtuo also runs a "Virtuo for Business" corporate program and has committed to offsetting 100% of trips and electrifying its fleet by 2030. Virtuo does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Leapmotor
providers.description: Leapmotor (Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology Co., Ltd., HKEX: 9863) is a Chinese intelligent electric vehicle manufacturer founded in 2015 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China, which sold its first vehicles in 2019. Leapmotor designs and builds battery-electric and range-extended (REEV) passenger vehicles — including the T03 city car and the B03X, B05, B10 and C10 SUVs — on its own vertically integrated LEAP platform, developing its electric drive, battery, and intelligent cockpit and driving systems in house. Stellantis took a stake in the company in 2023 and, through the Leapmotor International joint venture, distributes Leapmotor vehicles across Europe and other export markets via leapmotor.net. Leapmotor operates connected-vehicle services — the Leapmotor mobile app, OTA software updates, and the Leapmotor Connected Experience — but publishes no public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation; the vehicle cloud interfaces used by its mobile app are private and only reached through unofficial, reverse-engineered community clients.

providers.name: Zero Motorcycles
providers.description: Zero Motorcycles is an American manufacturer of electric motorcycles and powertrains, founded in 2006 in Santa Cruz, California. It designs and builds street, dual-sport and off-road electric motorcycles across its S, DS, FX and X lines — including the SR/S, SR/F, DSR/X, FXE and XE — around a proprietary Z-Force electric powertrain and aircraft-grade aluminum frame. Its bikes run the Cypher operating system, which pairs with the Zero Motorcycles NextGen mobile app over Bluetooth and cellular telematics for ride data, remote diagnostics, over-the-air updates and performance customization, and with the Cypher Store, where owners purchase software upgrades that unlock additional power, top speed and features. Zero sells internationally through a dealer network and serves retail, fleet and authority/first-responder segments. Its connected-vehicle platform is consumer-facing only: Zero publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Claim Genius
providers.description: Claim Genius is an AI vehicle-inspection and automated damage-assessment company serving auto insurance claims, underwriting, dealerships, salvage, lease and rental, fleet and collision repair. Its GeniusINSPECT engine converts vehicle photos and video into structured, decision-ready data — per-part damage classification (scratch, dent, tear, glass, wheel), repair-versus-replace decisions, labor and paint hours, OEM part pricing, repairability status and total-loss probability. The capabilities are packaged as products (GeniusINSPECT for Claims, GeniusINSPECT for Underwriting, GeniusPrepost, GeniusOPS) and exposed to integrators through the GeniusAPI Suite, a JWT-authenticated REST API with asynchronous pipeline processing. The company has operated across the US, EU and Asia since 2018.

providers.name: Mia
providers.description: Mia (Mia Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered phone agent platform built specifically for automotive dealerships. Its conversational voice AI answers calls 24/7 across sales, service, reception, and outbound operations, handling appointment scheduling, service booking, lead capture, and recall/follow-up outreach over phone, SMS, and voice with automatic multi-language detection. Mia integrates with major dealership platforms and DMS/CRM systems including Tekion, CDK, Reynolds & Reynolds, and Dealertrack, and reports use across 350+ dealerships. The company raised a $20M Series A (roughly $29M total) backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Permanent Capital Ventures. This profile currently covers the company identity; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Aptiv
providers.description: Aptiv is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Aptiv API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Carmoola
providers.description: Carmoola is a UK-based, mobile-first car finance platform that lets consumers get a pre-approved budget in minutes through its app, then pay dealers or private sellers directly with a virtual card. It offers Hire Purchase (HP) and Personal Contract Purchase (PCP) financing, soft credit checks that do not affect the applicant's score, flexible repayment terms, and the ability to refinance an existing car loan. Carmoola is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and is backed by investors including QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Carmoola operates a consumer app rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: CarOnSale
providers.description: CarOnSale is an AI-supported B2B marketplace for used-car trading across Europe, operated by Castle Tech GmbH. Licensed dealers, OEMs, fleet operators, and leasing companies buy and sell used vehicles through digital auctions built on standardized 110-point condition assessments, AI-based pricing and valuation, and integrated transport and financing services. The platform connects sellers (dealer groups, OEMs, leasing and rental companies) with a European network of professional buyers, handling procurement, price discovery, settlement, and logistics end to end. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Donut Media
providers.description: Donut Media is an American automotive entertainment brand and one of the largest automotive channels on YouTube, founded in 2015 by Matt Levin, Ben Conrad, and Nick Moceri. It is best known for original series such as Up to Speed, Money Pit, and HiLow, along with the Past Gas podcast, reaching millions of car enthusiasts through video, social, and audio. Donut monetizes through advertising, brand sponsorships, content licensing, and an extensive Shopify-powered online store selling apparel, hats, and collectibles. The company was acquired by Recurrent Ventures in November 2021. This profile documents Donut Media's public web and commerce surface; the company does not publish a developer API program.

providers.name: Kardome Technology
providers.description: Kardome develops Voice AI technology that lets voice-integrated products hear and understand speech with human-level accuracy in complex, real-world acoustic environments. Its two core technologies are Spatial Hearing AI, which understands the acoustic scene to localize sound sources and attribute speech to the correct speaker, and Cognition AI, which adds contextual awareness so devices understand what people mean in the moment. Kardome targets automotive in-car voice UI and smart-home voice interaction in noisy environments. The company is a Techstars portfolio company, tracked in the API Evangelist network; it licenses embedded voice technology to device makers rather than publishing a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Moj.io
providers.description: Mojio (moj.io) is a connected-car and connected-mobility platform that collects, processes, and monetizes vehicle telematics data at scale for mobile network operators, automotive OEMs, insurers, and fleet/field-service businesses. Its "Mobility Studio" platform exposes REST endpoints for vehicle data, a PUSH API for real-time insights, mobile SDKs, and a vehicle simulator, alongside a white-label consumer app (Motion) and a services ecosystem (Alexa, Google Maps, Bosch, and others). Mojio has processed 15+ billion miles of driving data. As of this pass the API and SDK surface is partner-gated — there is no public developer portal, published OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Preteckt
providers.description: Preteckt provides AI-powered predictive maintenance for transit buses, coach buses, and trucking fleets. Its platform ingests vehicle sensor telemetry and applies machine-learning algorithms to detect maintenance issues before they cause breakdowns, reducing diagnostic time by nearly 50 percent and preventing roughly 20 percent of failures. Preteckt processes more than one million sensor data points per day per vehicle across 20+ maintenance-focused algorithms. The company is part of Diesel Laptops. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Preteckt publishes no public developer, API, documentation, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: Divergent
providers.description: Divergent Technologies, Inc. is a Torrance and Long Beach, California manufacturer that built the Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS), an end-to-end software-hardware production system for industrial digital manufacturing. DAPS pairs AI-driven generative design software with in-house metal additive manufacturing — the Monolith One printer, compatible with aluminum, nickel, steel and titanium alloys — and automated fixtureless robotic assembly, so complex multi-part structures can be engineered, printed and assembled without fixed tooling. Founded in 2013 by Kevin and Lukas Czinger, the company is a Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and has expanded into aerospace and defense, including selection under the US Air Force Eglin Wide Agile Acquisition Contract. Divergent sells manufactured structures and production capacity, not software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: CarServ
providers.description: CarServ was auto repair shop management software — marketed as "the operating system for auto repair" — used by single-site shops and multi-location repair groups to run repair orders, Digital Vehicle Inspections, technician and service advisor workflows, customer communication and payments. The company was backed by Techstars. It is no longer operating: carserv.com returned HTTP 410 Gone through late 2024 and now resolves to a registrar parking page delegated to Afternic name servers. CarServ shipped a read-only JSON:API v2 "Public API" covering repair orders, customers, vehicles, appointments, inspections, operations and their part, labor and sublet line items, authenticated by exchanging an API key and secret for a JWT bearer token. No OpenAPI definition, developer portal or documentation survives; this profile reconstructs the historical API contract from the company's own open-source Ruby client library, which remains public on GitHub.

providers.name: Motorq
providers.description: Motorq is a connected vehicle intelligence platform that taps native OEM connectivity to deliver AI-powered insights across the automotive ecosystem. It aggregates and normalizes vehicle telematics data from 25+ automotive brands and third-party sources without plug-in hardware or dongles, so fleets, fleet management companies, dealerships, lenders, insuretechs, and mobility companies can drive maintenance, safety, utilization, and EV use cases. Motorq offers access through a cloud fleet management portal, bi-directional APIs and data streams (Get Location, Create Geofence, and more), and a Snowflake data lake integration. Its Motorq Fuse AI layer surfaces prioritized recommendations ranked by severity and cost impact. API access is gated to enterprise and OEM partners; there is no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Seurat Technologies
providers.description: Seurat Technologies is a Wilmington, Massachusetts contract manufacturer that produces high-volume metal parts using its proprietary Area Printing technology, a Laser Powderbed Fusion (LPBF) additive process that decouples print speed from resolution and is positioned as roughly 10x more productive than conventional LPBF. Seurat does not sell 3D printers; it sells parts, qualifying customer designs through its Area Printing Production (APP) qualification program and then mass-producing them at localized factories for consumer electronics, automotive, energy, aerospace and defense OEMs. The company markets its process on reshoring, supply-chain resilience, tariff resistance and decarbonization, and engages customers through a quote / upload-your-part motion rather than any developer-facing product.

providers.name: EAS Innovations Inc
providers.description: EAS Innovations Inc operates ELEV8, an end-to-end, cloud-based dealer management system (DMS) built for independent auto dealers and automotive finance companies. The platform unifies real-time accounting, inventory management, CRM and desking, loan servicing, payments and collections into a single fully-integrated system. It offers per-seat pricing, user-based access rights, user-level audit logs, whitelisted IP addresses, multi-rooftop access and department-level restrictions, and is delivered as a SaaS web application at app.elev8dms.com. EAS Innovations is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: FordPass / Ford Pro
providers.description: FordPass is Ford Motor Company's consumer connected-vehicle mobile app and service platform for Ford and Lincoln owners, exposing remote start/stop, remote lock/unlock, vehicle status (fuel/charge, tire pressure, oil life, odometer, location), Vehicle Health alerts, BlueCruise hands-free driving, Wi-Fi hotspot, Phone As A Key, scheduled service, and roadside assistance via the embedded FordPass Connect 4G LTE modem. Ford Pro is Ford's commercial fleet brand spanning Ford Pro Telematics, Ford Pro Intelligence, Ford Pro E-Telematics for EVs, Ford Pro Charging, Ford Pro FinSimple, and dealer/upfit services. The Ford Developer Marketplace (developer.ford.com) hosts Ford's partner-facing API program — FordConnect Query API for consumer-vehicle data and remote command access (with vehicle-owner consent via FordPass account OAuth), plus a Ford Pro REST API surface for fleets including Vehicle Status, Vehicle Historical Status, Vehicle Metadata, Vehicle Efficiency (fuel/energy/idle), Driver Behavior, Trip Reports, and Vehicle Health. Ford Pro Telematics is integrated with Geotab, Fleetio, Samsara, Motive, Verizon Connect, and other fleet platforms, and Smartcar offers a consumer OAuth bridge to Ford vehicles using FordPass Connect credentials. Access to Ford APIs is gated behind a partner application and credentials issued through the Ford Developer Portal; Ford has periodically restricted individual-developer access. No public OpenAPI specification is published outside the partner portal, so this profile documents the Ford developer surface as an index without a generated machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Guazi
providers.description: Guazi is a China-based used-car export, auction, and trading platform founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing. It connects international dealers and buyers with used vehicles sourced across China, offering sealed-bid online auctions, Buy It Now direct sales, a 200-plus-point vehicle inspection process, direct sourcing on request, and global logistics shipping to more than 50 countries via container and Ro-Ro. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, HongShan (Sequoia China), and Tencent, Guazi handles over 200,000 vehicles annually. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence; no public developer program, API, or SDK has been found.

providers.name: NNG
providers.description: NNG (NNG Software Developing and Commercial LLC), formerly Nav N Go, is a Budapest-based automotive navigation and location-based software company founded in 2004. Its flagship iGO platform delivers modular guidance, positioning, routing, map content management, and driver-assistance features such as Intelligent Speed Assistance, embedded in more than 60 million devices across 30+ vehicle brands and supplied to over 150 automotive and mobility partners in nearly 200 countries. NNG is backed by growth investment from Insight Partners. NNG sells embedded and OEM location-based software rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: PitPro Automation
providers.description: PitPro Automation is a fleet-maintenance technology company building automated tire-service systems that perform full tire changes and rotations on commercial fleet vehicles in under fifteen minutes. Targeting Class 2 and smaller vehicles, the company serves last-mile delivery, rideshare, utility, telecom, moving, and government fleets with in-bay automation, 24/7 monitoring, and field support. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, PitPro is a hardware-and-software provider focused on reducing fleet downtime; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: A. Schulman
providers.description: A. Schulman was a global supplier of high-performance plastic compounds, composites, and powders used by manufacturers across packaging, automotive, electronics, and consumer goods industries. The company was acquired by LyondellBasell in 2018 and now operates as the Advanced Polymer Solutions division, continuing to supply engineered plastics, masterbatches, compounds, and specialty powders to global manufacturers.

providers.name: Rivian Automotive
providers.description: Rivian Automotive is an American electric vehicle manufacturer that designs and builds adventure-oriented electric trucks, SUVs, and commercial delivery vans, along with the charging infrastructure and connected-vehicle software that supports them. While Rivian does not publish a public developer API portal, an unofficial GraphQL API powers the Rivian mobile app and has been reverse-engineered by community projects for vehicle telemetry and control.

providers.name: Spartan Radar
providers.description: Spartan Radar is an automotive radar software and sensing company, now operating as the radar technology brand of Pro-Vision Solutions, LLC following its 2025 acquisition. Its Clarify software applies proprietary digital signal processing and machine-learning perception to existing automotive radar sensors, raising resolution 3-8x on commodity silicon (ARM Cortex, Texas Instruments TDA4VM and AWR, NVIDIA Orin and DRIVE, NXP SAF85xx/SAF86xx) without new hardware, and its Hoplo product is a software-defined collision-avoidance and blind-spot warning system for commercial and heavy vehicles across mining, construction, material handling and logistics. Spartan sells to commercial-vehicle OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers and fleet operators as embedded software and hardware; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Voya
providers.description: Voya GmbH is a software development and consulting company based in Hamburg, Germany, with nearshore TechHubs in Bucharest and Cluj, Romania. Founded in 2015 as an AI-powered chat-based business-travel booking platform backed by 500 Global, it became a wholly-owned Volkswagen Group subsidiary and has been an independent, founder-led company again since November 2024. Today Voya delivers end-to-end software development, applied AI solutions, and engineering team building for automotive, mobility, and travel clients including Volkswagen, Audi, CARIAD, Deutsche Bahn, and Lufthansa City Center. TISAX certified. Voya publishes no public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Kinetic
providers.description: Kinetic (Kinetic Automation) builds robotics-based automated collision repair for modern vehicles equipped with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The company operates robotic repair facilities (Kinetic Hubs), automated imaging for collision damage assessment and repair estimates (Kinetic Vision), and AI-powered calibration identification software (Kinetic ID) that determines which ADAS sensors need recalibration after a repair. Backed by Menlo Ventures and Techstars, Kinetic was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and corporate site plus a login-only identity portal (id.kinetic.auto); it exposes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhooks surface.

providers.name: Motorway
providers.description: Motorway is the UK's fastest-growing used car marketplace, connecting private sellers with a network of more than 8,000 verified car dealers through a daily online auction. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in London and Brighton, the platform provides instant AI-assisted vehicle valuations, a mobile app that builds a sale-ready car profile, nationwide home collection, same-day payment (Motorway Pay), transport (Motorway Move), and outstanding-finance handling. Over one million people have used Motorway to sell a car. It is a consumer and dealer (B2C/B2B) marketplace rather than a public API provider: no developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface is published as of this enrichment pass. Backed by Index Ventures, ICONIQ Growth, BMW i Ventures and LocalGlobe.

providers.name: Pebble
providers.description: Pebble is a Silicon Valley electric-vehicle and consumer-hardware company that designs and manufactures the Pebble Flow, an all-electric travel trailer (RV) with an integrated battery, solar, and motor-assist drivetrain. The product line pairs the trailer with the Pebble mobile app for remote control and monitoring, offering features such as autonomous "Magic Hitch" coupling, remote-control positioning, automatic leveling and setup, and up to seven days of off-grid capability. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pebble sells direct-to-consumer under the tagline "Where Home Meets the Road." As of this enrichment pass Pebble publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; its only software touchpoint is the consumer-facing Pebble Control Center app.

providers.name: CarSwitch
providers.description: CarSwitch is a tech-enabled used-car marketplace founded in Dubai in 2016 that facilitates buying and selling of pre-owned vehicles across the United Arab Emirates (Dubai, Abu Dhabi and nationwide) and Saudi Arabia. Rather than a traditional classifieds site, CarSwitch operates as a fully managed service: every car undergoes a 200-point inspection before listing, sellers get an end-to-end managed selling service (professional photography, listing, negotiation and RTA transfer handling), and buyers get price transparency, a free online car-valuation tool and installment financing through banking partners such as Emirates NBD, FAB, ADCB, ADIB, DIB and Emirates Islamic. The company has inspected 130,000+ vehicles and facilitated over $500 million in sales. CarSwitch was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer marketplace with no public developer API program.

providers.name: CarWale
providers.description: CarWale is an Indian automotive marketplace and part of CarTrade Tech Limited, connecting car buyers with new-car dealers and used-car sellers across 1,500+ cities in India. The consumer platform offers new and used vehicle listings, accurate on-road pricing sourced directly from dealers, car valuation and sell-car tools, side-by-side comparisons, expert reviews and first-drive reports, and automotive news and video content. CarWale reports over 34 million monthly unique visitors and operates alongside sister brands including BikeWale, CarTrade, CarWale abSure, Mobility Outlook, and Adroit Auto. CarWale does not currently publish a public developer portal or API; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Custodian
providers.description: Custodian (getcustodian.com) is a Mexico City-based consumer mobile application and insurtech service that centralizes vehicle documentation and automotive administrative tasks. The app helps drivers organize and store important paperwork, track expiration dates for registration, insurance policies, and health certificates, receive renewal notifications, and get assistance with auto-insurance renewals and claims management. A premium annual subscription (450 MXN) adds full document-handling and verification services (including Mexico City vehicle verification). Custodian is a consumer app distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Sweater
providers.description: Sweater (سويتر) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand mobile car-care company that brings waterless vehicle washing, interior cleaning, detailing, and fragrance services to customers wherever their car is parked. Its app-based platform uses smart scheduling to dispatch field teams by location and uses roughly 7 liters of water per wash versus about 120 liters for traditional methods. The company reports 2M+ washes, 750K+ users, 500+ corporate partnerships, and operations across 8 Saudi cities (Riyadh, Dammam, Khobar, Jeddah, Jubail, Medina, Al-Hassa, and Mecca). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer/B2B services business with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Achates Power
providers.description: Achates Power is a San Diego, California engine technology company founded in 2004 by Dr. James Lemke and John Walton that develops opposed-piston, two-stroke compression-ignition engine architecture and licenses the resulting engine designs, development tools, simulation software and patents to engine manufacturers and OEMs. Its engines target passenger vehicles, medium and heavy-duty commercial trucks, military vehicles, and off-road and power-generation applications, and the company has claimed fuel-efficiency improvements of as much as 30 percent over conventional engines at comparable or better emissions. Achates Power has received U.S. Army TARDEC, Department of Energy and ARPA-E funding and partners with engine manufacturers such as Fairbanks Morse. It is a privately held hardware and engineering licensing business and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Lumotive
providers.description: Lumotive is a Seattle-based semiconductor company building programmable optics on its patented Light Control Metasurface (LCM) technology — solid-state, software-defined beam steering implemented in a standard CMOS process with no moving parts. Its products include the LM10 and LX10 LCM beam-steering chips, the LCM Evaluation Kit (LEK), the M30 iToF and NM120 3D-sensing development kits, and the M30/TX10 reference designs, applied to industrial automation, intelligent traffic systems, automotive ADAS and autonomy, defense, and optical circuit switching for AI data centers. Lumotive publishes an "Open Lidar API" — a real-time control interface for software-defined Lidar 2.0 hardware covering region-of-interest scanning, frame rate, resolution and range, plus a common point-cloud format — and ships C/C++ LCM control libraries with Python bindings alongside its evaluation kits. That interface is an embedded hardware-control API, not a public web API: no developer portal, documentation site, machine-readable specification, or self-service sign-up is published, and access is granted to selected partners through the Technology Access Program by contacting the company.

providers.name: Tower International
providers.description: Tower International was a global manufacturer of engineered structural metal components and assemblies for the automotive industry, primarily serving original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). The company supplied body-structure stampings, frame and chassis structures, and complex welded assemblies for cars, crossovers, pickups, and SUVs. Tower International was acquired by Autokiniton Global Group in 2019 and merged with L&W Group to form the second largest Body-in-White and vehicle frame supplier in North America. As a private manufacturing company with no public developer API offering, Tower International does not expose public REST or web APIs.

providers.name: AK Steel Holding
providers.description: AK Steel Holding Corporation was a leading producer of flat-rolled carbon, stainless, and electrical steel products, as well as carbon and stainless tubular products, primarily serving the automotive, infrastructure, manufacturing, and electrical power markets. AK Steel was acquired by Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. in March 2020 and now operates as a subsidiary.

providers.name: Corning
providers.description: Corning Incorporated is a Fortune 500 American technology company that specializes in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics. Founded in 1851, Corning manufactures specialty glass, ceramics, and related materials and technologies for industrial and scientific applications. Corning's businesses include Optical Communications (fiber optic cable and hardware), Display Technologies (LCD and OLED glass substrates), Specialty Materials (Gorilla Glass for mobile devices), Environmental Technologies (ceramic substrates and filters for emissions control), and Life Sciences (laboratory glassware, cell culture, and bioprocess products). Corning does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: AutoNation
providers.description: AutoNation is the largest automotive retailer in the United States, operating over 250 new and used vehicle franchises along with collision centers, parts and service operations, and AutoNation USA used-vehicle stores. The company sells vehicles across most major OEM brands and provides digital retail, financing, and service scheduling capabilities through its website and mobile applications.

providers.name: Hugo
providers.description: Hugo is a mobile-first, usage-based car insurance company that lets drivers turn coverage on and off from their phone and pay in short intervals rather than a large upfront down payment. Through the Hugo app and web portal, customers can activate liability or comprehensive coverage in minutes, get instant proof of insurance, auto-reload their balance, and extend protection as needed. Hugo positions itself as a modern, micropayment alternative to traditional insurers for budget-conscious and gig-economy drivers, and is a seed-stage InsurTech company backed by Canaan Partners. Hugo operates in select U.S. states with expansion underway. Hugo is a consumer insurance application and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Bliq
providers.description: Bliq is a Berlin-based premium driverless-car subscription service rolling out across Europe. Instead of owning a car or paying per ride, members subscribe monthly to a private autonomous vehicle that Bliq charges, cleans, insures, maintains, and parks on their behalf. Cars are booked for time windows (hours or days) rather than single trips, every journey is remotely supervised by licensed local operators, and there is no surge pricing. Backed by Speedinvest, Bliq positions itself as "ownership without ownership." The company currently operates a consumer marketing site with early-access and waitlist flows and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Turo
providers.description: Turo is a San Francisco-headquartered peer-to-peer car sharing marketplace operating in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, and Australia. The platform lets vehicle owners (hosts) list their cars for rent and lets travelers (guests) book those vehicles directly through the Turo app or website, with Turo handling identity verification, insurance, protection plans, payments, and trust and safety on top of the host's inventory. The marketplace covers economy cars, SUVs, trucks, vans, exotic and classic vehicles, and EVs across more than 14,000 cities, and offers contactless Turo Go vehicles where supported. Turo's revenue model is a marketplace take-rate against each trip plus protection plan and ancillary fees, supported by an integrated host operations stack (calendar, pricing, messaging, and earnings) and a guest mobile and web booking experience. Turo does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or partner developer portal. The only third-party-facing surface was a now-deprecated ChatGPT plugin (chatgpt.turo.com) launched in 2023 and sunset alongside OpenAI's plugins program in 2024. Integrations with connected-car platforms such as Smartcar are negotiated directly rather than through self-serve developer onboarding, and Turo's public GitHub presence (github.com/turo, github.com/open-turo) is limited to internal engineering tooling, GitHub Actions, ESLint configs, and language-specific libraries rather than a public marketplace API.

providers.name: 1hai
providers.description: eHi Car Rental (一嗨租车), operated by Shanghai eHi Information Technology Services Co., Ltd., is one of China's leading car rental and mobility companies. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Shanghai, eHi offers self-drive car rentals, chauffeured car service, used-car sales, and corporate and government mobility programs across more than 500 cities nationwide, with cross-city return and airport pickup. eHi is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. The business operates consumer web and mobile (iOS, Android, HarmonyOS) booking channels; no public developer or API platform was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Autoliv
providers.description: Autoliv is the world's largest automotive safety supplier, designing, manufacturing, and selling airbags, seatbelts, steering wheels, inflators, pyrotechnic actuators, and related safety electronics for vehicle manufacturers worldwide. The company operates in 25 countries with 13 technology centers and serves all major OEMs.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Acerta Analytics
providers.description: Acerta (Acerta Analytics Solutions Inc.) is an industrial AI company whose LinePulse platform applies machine learning to real-time discrete-manufacturing production data to detect and resolve quality defects early. It helps automotive and manufacturing teams reduce scrap, rework, and end-of-line testing while protecting throughput, ingesting data from MES, PLC, and QMS systems and deploying in under 30 days. Surfaced as an EQT Ventures portfolio company; no public developer API or documentation is exposed today (data connectivity is via a private ingestion API and prebuilt integrations such as ETQ and Microsoft).

providers.name: AutoChilango
providers.description: AutoChilango (Auto Chilango) is a Mexico City-based mobile application that consolidates the everyday services drivers in CDMX and the State of Mexico need into a single app. It covers the "Hoy No Circula" driving-restriction calendar, vehicular verification schedules, traffic fines (multas) lookup and payment, annual registration (tenencia), insurance, parking, gas stations, and mechanical services for private cars, motorcycles, taxis, and special plates. Backed by 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer/API surface has been found, so this profile captures the provider's identity, information surface (blog, FAQs, privacy), and probed domain security.

providers.name: Upshift
providers.description: Upshift is a San Francisco fractional car subscription service — "a 2-car garage, in your pocket." Members choose 4, 8, or 12 driving days a month and get a premium Toyota hybrid delivered clean, fueled, insured, and maintained, then picked up when they are done, with plans from $399/month including insurance, delivery, and maintenance. A 500 Global and URBAN-X portfolio company, Upshift publishes no public developer program or API surface; the member experience runs through its iOS/Android apps and go.upshiftcars.com.

providers.name: ClearMotion
providers.description: ClearMotion is an automotive motion-technology company founded out of MIT in 2012 by Zack Anderson and Shakeel Avadhany, headquartered at its US innovation lab in Billerica, Massachusetts, with a UK engineering hub at MIRA Technology Park in Nuneaton, a Shanghai office, and a production plant in Changshu, China. Its CM1 fully active suspension system pairs the ActiValve digital hydraulic actuator with software that counteracts road disturbances in milliseconds, and its RoadMotion service is a crowdsourced, cloud-based road-surface intelligence layer that fuses data from vehicle sensors into a high-definition surface map accurate to better than 20mm, feeding proactive suspension, chassis and ADAS decisions. The company absorbed the Bose Ride and Project Sound active-suspension programs, is led by CEO Christian Steinmann, and ships with NIO (ET9, ES9) alongside collaborations with Porsche, BWI Group and Sona Comstar. Marketing material describes RoadMotion as an "end-to-end cloud API solution", but ClearMotion publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDKs or /.well-known discovery surface — the API is an OEM/B2B integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Zeromatter
providers.description: Zeromatter is a deep-tech simulation platform that lets teams build, test, and train autonomous systems in one environment. It provides high-performance sensor simulation, automatic environment generation, and multi-agent co-simulation frameworks used to accelerate development across autonomy, aerospace, automotive, agriculture, drones, and green energy. Backed by Spark Capital, Zeromatter currently exposes a marketing and company site only; no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a lead pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Apex.AI
providers.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Mips
providers.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

providers.name: Thor Industries
providers.description: Thor Industries is the world's largest manufacturer of recreational vehicles, owning subsidiary brands including Airstream, Jayco, Heartland RV, Keystone RV, and others. Thor Industries operates primarily as a manufacturing company and does not publish a public developer API. Dealer integrations and connected vehicle features are managed through subsidiary brands and OEM partnerships.

providers.name: Brazilian Vehicles and Prices
providers.description: Vehicles information from Fundação Instituto de Pesquisas Econômicas - Fipe

providers.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
providers.description: Cleveland-Cliffs is North America's largest flat-rolled steel producer and supplier of iron ore pellets, operating an integrated business spanning mining, steelmaking, and downstream finishing for the automotive, infrastructure, and manufacturing markets. Cleveland-Cliffs does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface. Programmatic interaction with the company is limited to investor and customer touchpoints (corporate website, investor relations, customer service, EDI for trading partners).

providers.name: Distance
providers.description: Distance (Distance Technologies) is a Helsinki-based frontier-tech company pioneering glasses-free extended reality (XR) built on computational optics and lightfield technology. Its systems turn transparent surfaces — vehicle windshields, aircraft canopies, and head-mounted visors — into intelligent heads-up displays without screens, overlays, or wearable glasses. Products include the Acuity visual-intelligence platform and Acuity OS for defense, the Field Operator HUD (FOH) head-mounted system in field trials across NATO countries, and panoramic lightfield HUDs for automotive ADAS and navigation. Distance is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and partners with defense, aerospace, and automotive organizations including Kia, Supacat, Galvion, Patria, and General Dynamics. The company publishes no public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Helipaddy sites
providers.description: Helicopter and passenger drone landing site directory, Helipaddy data and much more

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: MotorMia
providers.description: MotorMia is an AI-powered automotive platform for car enthusiasts, built around Mia, an AI modding partner, build advisor, and performance analyst. Users add their vehicles, set build and performance goals, and Mia returns personalized upgrade recommendations across engine, transmission, brakes, suspension, cooling, and exhaust systems, tuned to the user's level of mechanical experience. The platform is backed by a proprietary automotive intelligence dataset combining over 5 million aftermarket parts, more than 50 million fitment records, and real-world enthusiast build behavior from 1M+ community projects, and ships as iOS and Android mobile apps plus a web store. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, MotorMia raised $8M led by investors including Lerer Hippeau and Seedcamp. As of this profile MotorMia is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface.
