providers.description: NHTSA Product Information Catalog and Vehicle Listing

providers.name: Oshkosh
providers.description: Oshkosh Corporation is a Fortune 500 industrial company that designs and builds purpose-built vehicles and vehicle bodies, including access equipment, defense vehicles, fire and emergency apparatus, refuse collection vehicles, and concrete mixers.

providers.name: ProLogium Technology
providers.description: ProLogium Technology Co., Ltd. is a Taiwanese energy-innovation company founded in 2006 that develops and manufactures next-generation solid-state lithium ceramic batteries built around a 100% ceramic separator. It commercialized its first solid-state cells in 2013, opened the world's first giga-level solid-state lithium ceramic battery plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan in 2024, and operates a European R&D center at Paris-Saclay with a planned gigafactory in Dunkirk, France. Its product lines span FLCB, PLCB and LLCB cells plus battery modules and packs, targeting electric vehicles, energy storage systems, robotics, and consumer and industrial applications. ProLogium is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sidecar
providers.description: Sidecar (side.cr) was added to the API Evangelist network as a Union Square Ventures portfolio lead. The side.cr domain today hosts a transportation news and information content platform (self-described as "building the largest transportation news source powered by everyday people"), covering ridesharing, driving, delivery, safety, and automotive topics for riders and drivers. It is a reader-facing editorial site, not a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, OpenAPI, or any /.well-known discovery surface. The name echoes the pioneering peer-to-peer Sidecar ridesharing company that Union Square Ventures backed and that wound down in 2015, but the current content site states no operational or corporate ties to that defunct service. This profile is retained as a company/lead record with no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Auto1
providers.description: AUTO1 Group is Europe's leading digital automotive platform for buying, selling, and financing used cars, headquartered in Berlin, Germany. It operates the B2B wholesale marketplace AUTO1.com (used by 60,000+ professional car dealers across 30+ European countries), the consumer retail brand Autohero, and the consumer purchasing service wirkaufendeinauto.de (with localized variants across Europe). The group combines inspection, logistics, documentation, and digital financing into an end-to-end remarketing and retail platform. AUTO1 Group publishes open-source engineering work through its auto1-oss GitHub organization, but does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or published API documentation; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and domain-security posture only. Surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Lucid Motors
providers.description: Lucid Motors is the consumer-vehicle brand of Lucid Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: LCID), a Newark, California–headquartered American luxury electric vehicle manufacturer. The company designs and manufactures high-performance battery-electric sedans and SUVs, with its flagship Lucid Air (Pure, Touring, Grand Touring, and Sapphire trims) and the Lucid Gravity SUV (Touring and Grand Touring), assembled at its AMP-1 factory in Casa Grande, Arizona. Lucid develops its own electric powertrain, battery, and software stack — including the Lucid UX in-vehicle experience, the Lucid mobile app, Lucid Assistant, and over-the-air updates — and operates a vertically integrated direct-to-consumer sales, financing, leasing, and service model across North America, Europe, and the Middle East, supported by a growing network of Lucid Studios, Service Centers, and DC fast charging partnerships. Lucid is majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF). Beyond consumer vehicles, Lucid licenses its powertrain and battery technology to other OEMs (notably Aston Martin) and supplies battery systems through its Lucid energy storage initiatives. Lucid Motors does not publish a public developer API portal, SDK, or OpenAPI specification; the Lucid mobile app and vehicle telematics are powered by private backend services that are not documented for third-party use.

providers.name: Sonic Automotive
providers.description: Sonic Automotive is one of the largest automotive retailers in the United States, operating 100+ franchise dealerships across 13 states representing 25+ automotive brands, and operating EchoPark Automotive used-vehicle stores. The company invests in digital retail, inventory management technology, and automotive data platforms to enhance customer experience across vehicle sales, service, finance, and insurance. Technology partners include Stripe, NETSOL, and CDK Global.

providers.name: Humanising Autonomy
providers.description: Humanising Autonomy is a London-based behavioural AI company that builds ethical computer-vision software to understand and predict human behaviour, providing context between people and machines. Its "Behaviour AI" platform combines novel deep learning, behavioural psychology and statistical AI to analyse existing camera and video footage across automotive & ADAS, fleet telematics, city infrastructure & planning, and health & safety use cases -- improving road safety and reducing liability. The company connects to a customer's existing cameras, platform or video footage rather than exposing a public developer API. Backed by Anthemis. NOTE: the primary website (humanisingautonomy.com) is currently unreachable / parked (HTTP 404) as of 2026-07-19, indicating the company may be inactive; this profile is reconstructed from archived (Wayback) sources -- no public API, SDK registry, or developer portal was ever published.

providers.name: Bitauto
providers.description: Bitauto (易车, Yiche) is one of China's largest automotive internet companies, founded in 2000 with the mission of making car ownership simpler. It operates consumer-facing platforms that provide car buyers with pricing, reviews, specifications, and automotive news across new and used vehicles, alongside an enterprise EP (dealer) platform offering web-based digital marketing and CRM applications to Chinese automobile dealers. Bitauto runs regional informational portals across 20+ countries cataloging Chinese car brands. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures; as of enrichment Bitauto publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cooper Standard Holdings
providers.description: Cooper Standard Holdings is a global automotive supplier headquartered in Northville, Michigan, that designs, engineers, manufactures, and sells sealing systems, fuel and brake delivery systems, and fluid transfer systems for global automotive original equipment manufacturers including Ford, General Motors, Stellantis, and Volkswagen. The company operates in approximately 20 countries with around 32,000 employees and is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker CPS. Cooper Standard does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence centers on corporate, investor, supplier, and careers websites.

providers.name: American Tire Distributors Holdings
providers.description: American Tire Distributors (ATD) is one of the largest independent suppliers of replacement tires in North America, distributing passenger, light truck, medium truck, and specialty tires from more than 110 distribution centers. ATD delivers over 30.5 million tire units annually to more than 85,000 delivery points across the United States and Canada, serving independent tire dealers, automotive service centers, and retailers.

providers.name: Audi Connect / myAudi
providers.description: Audi Connect is the connected-vehicle services platform from Audi AG, the Ingolstadt, Germany-based luxury automaker and member of the Volkswagen Group. Delivered to drivers through the embedded MMI infotainment system and the myAudi companion app for iOS and Android, Audi Connect spans remote vehicle control (lock/unlock, remote start, climate pre-conditioning, EV charge management), safety and security (Emergency Call/eCall, Audi Service Request, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing, speed alerts), and in-car infotainment (real-time traffic, satellite map imagery, parking and fuel information, weather, news, natural voice recognition, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Music, Wi-Fi hotspot, and an in-vehicle app store with Disney+ and passenger gaming on supported models). Services are packaged as Audi connect CARE (included for ten years on new U.S. Audis), Audi connect NAV (navigation and live traffic), and Audi connect PLUS (premium streaming and Wi-Fi). For EVs and PHEVs, Audi Connect adds charging-station search, remote charge monitoring, and cabin pre-conditioning. Audi does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, OAuth program, or partner SDK for myAudi/Audi Connect; programmatic access today is brokered by third-party connected-car aggregators (Smartcar, High Mobility, Enode, Mojio) under Audi's commercial agreements, and community projects reverse-engineer the mobile-app endpoints. Audi has publicly discussed an internal OpenAPI-driven API management strategy (with Nagarro) but the surface remains private to Audi, VW Group brands, and authorized partners.

providers.name: Commsignia
providers.description: Commsignia is a Budapest-based V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) technology company building connected vehicle and smart infrastructure solutions for the automotive and transportation industries. Its portfolio spans roadside units (RSUs) and onboard units (OBUs), a V2X software stack, and cloud services grouped into product suites: Roadway Intelligence, Emergency Safety, Fleet, Automotive, Smart Infrastructure, and Connected Vehicle. The company turns isolated roadway and vehicle data silos into real-world operational intelligence for safer roads and improved traffic flow. As of this enrichment pass Commsignia publishes no public developer API, REST/OpenAPI reference, SDK, or developer portal; technical integration is handled through direct engagement. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: Source.dev
providers.description: Source.dev builds AI-native software tooling that helps device manufacturers develop, build, and update the operating systems that run intelligent devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles. Its platform virtualizes source access (SourceFS) to cut Android checkout-and-build times from hours to minutes, replays build steps across languages and systems for faster CI, and uses LLM-driven merging (Harmony AI / Continuous Merges) to automatically resolve conflicts when applying security patches and OS upgrades to large, long-lived codebases like AOSP. The company is a sales/demo-led platform for device makers and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface.

providers.name: Ossia
providers.description: Ossia, Inc. is a Redmond, Washington wireless power technology company founded by physicist Hatem Zeine (incorporated as Omnilectric in 2008, operating as Ossia from 2013) and the inventor of Cota Real Wireless Power — a patented RF smart-antenna system that delivers targeted energy over the air to multiple moving devices at a distance, without pads, plugs, cables or line of sight. A Cota receiver emits a beacon and the Cota transmitter returns a focused 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz power signal along the same path, which is how the system tracks and powers devices in motion. Ossia does not manufacture products for sale: it licenses the Cota technology to manufacturers, brands and OEMs, ships Cota developer and reference design kits (receiver chip, sample hardware, software components, test instructions) to authorized licensees, and works through joint ventures and development partners such as Motherson Ossia. The company holds 180+ US and international patents, is FCC certified under Parts 15 and 18, and carries regulatory approval in the US, UK and 45+ other countries. Ossia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — the developer surface it does have is hardware and firmware delivered under license.

providers.name: StoneEagle F&I
providers.description: StoneEagle F&I is an automotive Finance & Insurance (F&I) technology company that has spent more than 35 years building the software backbone of dealership F&I operations. Its product suite spans Variable Ops (StoneEagleMENU, an electronic F&I menu-selling and product-presentation system, and StoneEagleMETRICS, real-time DMS-sourced sales and F&I reporting), Fixed Ops (PENCILWRENCH and StoneEagleMETRICS SERVICE for the service drive), and industry benchmarking (StoneEagleDATA, transaction-level insight across more than half of U.S. franchised dealers). StoneEagle connects to dealerships through certified DMS integrations and partners such as Dealertrack and F&I Express, but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal — integration is delivered as private, certified dealer and partner connections. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Uxin
providers.description: Uxin (优信) is a Chinese used-car e-commerce company backed by DCM Ventures. It operates the xin.com consumer used-car retail marketplace and the Youxinpai (优信拍) B2B online used-car auction and trading platform that connects dealers with buyers, including vehicle listings, auctions, logistics, and post-sale services. Uxin publishes no public developer portal or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Automatic
providers.description: Automatic (Automatic Labs, Inc.) was a San Francisco connected-car company founded in 2011 by Thejo Kote and Jerry Jariyasunant. Its OBD-II adapter and companion mobile app turned almost any car built since 1996 into a connected car, adding trip logging, fuel and MPG tracking, engine-light diagnostics, parking recall, and automatic crash alerts. Automatic ran a public developer platform at developer.automatic.com built around three surfaces: a REST API exposing trip, user, and vehicle data; an Events API delivering real-time driving events such as ignition on/off, hard braking, acceleration, speeding, and location changes over webhooks and websockets; and a private-beta Streaming SDK that read raw OBD-II data from the second-generation adapter over Bluetooth. SiriusXM acquired the company on 2017-04-27 for approximately $115 million, and all operations were shut down on 2020-05-28. THIS COMPANY IS DEFUNCT — no API, developer portal, or documentation remains online, and the automatic.com domain now belongs to the unrelated company Automattic. This profile is retained as a historical record of a notable connected-car API platform.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Nexu
providers.description: Nexu is a Mexico City fintech that provides automotive financing at the point of sale. Founded in 2014 by Abdon Nacif and Fernando Gomez Arriola, the company began as an auto price and comparison site and now operates a digital lending platform used by car dealerships across Mexico to originate credit and leasing offers in real time. Nexu underwrites and funds two consumer products - credito automotriz (auto credit) and arrendamiento (leasing with a purchase option and no residual), distributed through partnerships with more than ten OEM dealer networks including Nissan, Volkswagen, Kia, Hyundai, Mazda, Honda, Ford, Chevrolet, BMW and Audi. Applicants complete an onboarding and identity flow in a browser application at nexu.mx and receive a decision without visiting a branch. The company has raised roughly $73M across five equity rounds, plus debt facilities, from Valor Capital Group, Altos Ventures, Wollef, Architect Capital, Clocktower, Tresalia Capital, FJ Labs, Gilgamesh Ventures and others. As of this profiling pass Nexu publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind - see x-coverage below.

providers.name: Numa
providers.description: Numa is the AI Operating System for car dealerships. Its voice AI and messaging platform answers dealership calls and texts, connects directly to the DMS (CDK, Tekion, Reynolds & Reynolds) with roughly 90% DMS coverage, books service appointments, and coordinates the service lane and fixed operations. Used by over 1,300 dealerships, Numa reports cutting average customer response time from 23 hours to under 10 minutes and lifting repair-order dollars per advisor. Numa publishes no public API or developer portal; integrations are delivered through native DMS, CRM, and scheduler connectors.

providers.name: Yoshi
providers.description: Yoshi Mobility is a mobile vehicle-care and fleet-services platform founded in 2015 (Y Combinator S16). It brings automotive services to the vehicle wherever it is parked: mobile maintenance and oil changes, car washes and detailing, tire and battery service, EV charging, and live-video vehicle inspections that produce API-ready, signed results for fleets and rideshare platforms. Yoshi originally pioneered on-demand fuel delivery (that division was acquired by EZFill Holdings in January 2025) and now concentrates on mobile auto care and inspection technology, backed by strategic investors including General Motors Ventures, Bridgestone, and ExxonMobil. Integrations and APIs are offered to partners through direct sales rather than a public self-service developer portal.

providers.name: Kaiser Aluminum
providers.description: Kaiser Aluminum manufactures semi-fabricated aluminum products for industrial applications across aerospace, packaging, general engineering, and automotive markets. The nearly century-old company delivers highly engineered aluminum products focused on strength, weight efficiency, and sustainability. Kaiser Online serves as a customer portal for quotes, order tracking, depot stock searches, and material certifications.

providers.name: BYD
providers.description: BYD Company Ltd. is a Chinese multinational manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Shenzhen, founded in 1995 by Wang Chuanfu and publicly listed in Hong Kong (1211) and Shenzhen (002594). Originally a rechargeable-battery maker, BYD has grown into one of the world's largest producers of new-energy vehicles (battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars, buses, and trucks), power batteries (including the Blade Battery), consumer and automotive electronics, rail transit systems (SkyRail/SkyShuttle), forklifts, and solar and energy-storage products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; BYD is a hardware and manufacturing company and does not publish a public developer or API program.

providers.name: ConvenientPower
providers.description: ConvenientPower (Chengdu ConvenientPower Semiconductor, 成都市易冲半导体有限公司) is an analog and mixed-signal integrated-circuit design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Silicon Valley. The company designs high-performance power-management ICs spanning the full link from 220V mains to battery: wireless-charging transmitters and receivers (Qi, up to 100W), USB Power Delivery and UFCS protocol controllers, AC/DC flyback and synchronous rectifier controllers, GaN-integrated solutions, battery-charging management, LDOs and DC/DC converters, and automotive-grade power ICs (wireless charging, LED lighting, eFuse protection, switches). Its parts ship into consumer electronics, accessories, and automotive markets, with more than 330 million units shipped and 160+ patents; automotive ICs are AEC-Q100 qualified. As a hardware semiconductor vendor, ConvenientPower exposes developer resources as chip SDK toolkits, reference designs, and design software rather than a public web API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Polestar
providers.description: Polestar is a Swedish premium electric performance car brand, originally spun out of Volvo Cars' Polestar Performance racing arm and now jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.

providers.name: Autobia
providers.description: Autobia is a B2B e-commerce marketplace for the automotive aftermarket in Saudi Arabia, connecting auto-parts retailers, workshops, and service centers with wholesalers and dealers. The platform offers real-time pricing and instant ordering across more than 20,000 spare parts from multiple brands, centralizing sourcing to streamline procurement and improve supply-chain efficiency for the automotive sector. Backed by Techstars, Autobia operates via a web platform and native iOS and Android apps. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Cooper Tire & Rubber
providers.description: Cooper Tire & Rubber Company is an American manufacturer of replacement tires for passenger cars, light trucks, SUVs, and commercial vehicles, founded in 1914 and headquartered in Findlay, Ohio. Cooper was acquired by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company in June 2021 and now operates as a subsidiary, retaining the Cooper brand alongside Goodyear. The Cooper brand portfolio covers all-season, winter, all-terrain, and sport performance tires distributed through retailers and dealers worldwide. Cooper Tire does not publish a public developer program or REST APIs. Its digital presence is consumer-facing tire selection, retailer locators, and post-purchase tire registration.

providers.name: Autonomic
providers.description: Autonomic is a connected-vehicle cloud company founded in 2016, acquired by Ford Motor Company in 2018 and fully integrated into Ford in 2023. Its flagship product, the Transportation Mobility Cloud (TMC), is one of the largest connected-vehicle cloud platforms in production, providing an API-driven platform for developers to build applications that interact with vehicles while abstracting the complexity of different vehicle models and connectivity devices. The public developer surface (the TMC Developer Portal) is gated behind partner authentication, so most technical artifacts are not publicly harvestable. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Craft Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Anywhere 2 Go
providers.description: Anywhere 2 Go Co., Ltd. is a Bangkok, Thailand insurtech company and the maker of Claim Di, a mobile application ecosystem that streamlines motor insurance claims and vehicle inspection between drivers, independent surveyors, and insurance companies. Its flagship "Shake and Go" (K4K) feature lets two Claim Di users resolve minor accidents on the spot, while Emergency Alert, self-service Car Inspection, photo-based Non-Accident Claims, and the Claim Di Bike surveyor-dispatch program cut claim processing time and help insurers reduce fraud. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. Claim Di is a consumer/B2B mobile product (iOS and Android); no public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Civil Maps
providers.description: Civil Maps was a San Francisco autonomous-vehicle mapping company founded in 2015 by Sravan Puttagunta and Scott Harvey, with Fabien Chraim and Anuj Gupta on the founding team. It built AI software that turned vehicle LiDAR and camera data into machine-readable HD 3D maps and delivered real-time six-degrees-of-freedom localization at 15-20 cm absolute accuracy, crowdsourcing map updates from production fleets rather than from dedicated survey vehicles, and packaged that as the Atlas DevKit and Atlas Lite DevKit car-mounted units. It raised roughly USD 17 million across four rounds, including a USD 6.6 million seed led by Motus Ventures with Ford Motor Company, Wicklow Capital, StartX and AME Cloud Ventures, and was acquired by Luminar Technologies in mid-2022 - an acquisition Luminar announced at CES in January 2023 and folded into its Sentinel platform. Civil Maps no longer operates as an independent business: civilmaps.com is a frozen four-page marketing archive stamped "Copyright 2019" with no developer section, it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its 2015-era GitHub organization holds five C++ repositories last pushed between 2017 and 2020.

providers.name: Clutch Canada
providers.description: Clutch is a Toronto-headquartered, vertically integrated online used-car retailer serving Canadian drivers. Unlike marketplace models that broker to third-party dealers, Clutch owns its own inventory and runs an end-to-end e-commerce purchase flow at clutch.ca: browsing reconditioned pre-owned vehicles, auto financing and a loan calculator, trade-in and sell-my-car offers, protection plans, insurance, and home delivery, backed by a 10-day money-back guarantee. It operates across Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is a consumer retail business rather than an API vendor: its software is shipped as an end-user web application, and it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Drivemate
providers.description: Drivemate is a peer-to-peer car-sharing and car-rental marketplace based in Bangkok, Thailand, founded in 2016. The platform lets vehicle owners list their cars and lets travelers and residents rent directly from those owners through the Drivemate mobile app and website, handling booking, verification, insurance and payments end to end. Drivemate operates one of the largest car-rental selections in Thailand with more than 3,000 vehicles across 35 provinces and a community of over 100,000 users, and has raised Series A funding from investors including 500 Global (500 Startups), NetSol, Isuzu UNT and Colopl Next. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public digital and developer surface; Drivemate is a consumer mobility marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API program, so this record captures identity, distribution and domain-security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Kelley Blue Book
providers.description: Vehicle info, pricing, configuration, plus much more

providers.name: TRW Automotive Holdings
providers.description: TRW Automotive Holdings was one of the world's largest automotive parts suppliers, specializing in active and passive safety systems including braking systems, steering systems, suspension systems, seat belts, airbags, and advanced driver assistance systems. TRW Automotive was acquired by ZF Friedrichshafen AG in 2015 and is now part of ZF Group, operating as ZF TRW. The company's automotive safety technologies are integrated across major global OEMs. TRW no longer operates an independent developer API program; developer and partner integrations are handled through ZF Group's partner ecosystem.

providers.name: BorgWarner
providers.description: BorgWarner is a global automotive supplier designing and manufacturing propulsion systems, thermal management, battery systems, charging solutions, and power electronics for combustion, hybrid, and electric vehicles. The company accelerates the world's transition to clean, efficient mobility across passenger and commercial vehicle markets.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: KAR Auction Services (Historical)
providers.description: KAR Auction Services was a leading provider of vehicle auction, vehicle remarketing, and salvage auction services in North America. The company divested its salvage business IAA in 2023 (now part of RB Global) and rebranded its remaining wholesale business as OPENLANE. This repository is retained for historical reference. For current activity see the OPENLANE repository.

providers.name: Kavak
providers.description: Kavak is a Mexico-founded digital marketplace for buying, selling, and financing pre-owned cars across Latin America, the Middle East, and Turkey. Founded in 2016 in Mexico City by Carlos Garcia Ottati, Loreanne Garcia Ottati, and Roger Laughlin, Kavak became Mexico's first unicorn in 2020 and reached an $8.7B valuation in 2021 with backing from SoftBank, Sea Ltd, and Founders Fund. The company operates an end-to-end consumer platform that combines an e-commerce site and mobile app, physical hubs, in-house vehicle reconditioning, and a financial-services arm (Kavak Capital, Kuna, and Kavak Credito). Internally, Kavak uses machine learning and proprietary pricing models to value, inspect, and route inventory across markets including Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, the United Arab Emirates, and Turkey, while sponsoring high-profile partners such as the NFL. Kavak's revenue comes from vehicle sales, financing margins, and after-sales services, and the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub organization. Customer-facing integrations are limited to the consumer web and mobile apps and partner financing channels.

providers.name: Lear
providers.description: Lear Corporation is a Fortune 500 global automotive technology leader in Seating and E-Systems, delivering complete seat systems, electrical distribution and connection systems, and intelligent in-vehicle technology to vehicles from major automakers worldwide. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: LKQ Corporation
providers.description: LKQ Corporation is a Fortune 500 company and a leading provider of alternative and specialty parts to repair and accessorize automobiles and other vehicles, with operations across North America, Europe, and Taiwan. LKQ does not currently expose a public developer portal or REST API; this repository captures publicly available company and partner-program references.

providers.name: Boson Motors
providers.description: Boson Motors is an electric vehicle and robotics company founded in 2017, building a modular electric off-road utility vehicle (UTV) platform for agriculture, farm automation, and work applications. Its flagship LX40 is a user-serviceable, low-maintenance electric 4WD UTV that charges from a standard 110v outlet and accepts interchangeable work modules for spraying, hauling, and crew transport. The company operates engineering and production out of Tada, Andhra Pradesh, India, with a strategic base in Fremont, California, and maintains a robotics arm (Boson Robotics) focused on autonomous and agricultural automation. Boson Motors is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer marketing and reservation site with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation; its public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of ROS/robotics libraries. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and enrichment target.

providers.name: Harman International
providers.description: Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is a global leader in connected technologies for automotive, consumer, and enterprise markets, including connected car systems, audio products, professional solutions, and connected services. Harman does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; integrations with Harman platforms (such as Ignite, Ready Connect, and audio brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, and AKG) are typically delivered through commercial partnerships and OEM agreements.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Pep Boys
providers.description: Pep Boys is an American automotive aftermarket service chain founded in 1921 and headquartered in Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania. Owned by Icahn Enterprises since 2016, Pep Boys completed its transition away from retail parts in December 2023 and now operates as a service-only chain with roughly 850 to 900+ service centers across the U.S. and Puerto Rico, including a Pep Boys Mobile Crew offering for fleet and on-location maintenance. Pep Boys does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: 1-Automotive
providers.description: 1-Automotive is a catalog entry for which no operating company, developer program, or live web presence could be verified. The only host this profile ever recorded, www.1-automotive.com, is not a registered domain — Verisign WHOIS returns "No match for domain 1-AUTOMOTIVE.COM" and DNS answers NXDOMAIN for both the apex and the www label (probed 2026-08-29) — so the Website pointer that stood here asserted a page that has never existed and has been removed. Public web search returns no organization trading under this exact name; the nearest real match, and the likely origin of this slug, is Group 1 Automotive (NYSE: GPI), the Fortune 500 automotive retailer that API Evangelist profiles separately under the group-1-automotive slug, where its live llms.txt vehicle-inventory surface is already captured. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP server, A2A agent card, SDK, package or developer portal exists for this entry, and none has been authored on its behalf.

providers.name: 2duche
providers.description: 2Duche was a Chinese used-car marketing and trading service platform, backed by Qiming Venture Partners and recognized on the Red Herring Asia 100 in 2009. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company appears defunct — the apex domain 2duche.com does not resolve and www.2duche.com is unreachable, with no discoverable developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or public code repositories. No API artifacts could be produced without fabrication.

providers.name: Autobutler
providers.description: Autobutler is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Automatic Labs
providers.description: Automatic Labs was a connected-car company (the Automatic OBD-II adapter and companion app plus a developer platform / REST API for trip, vehicle, and driving-behavior data), founded circa 2011 and backed by a16z. It was acquired by SiriusXM in 2017 and wound down: the service and its developer API were discontinued around May 2020. As of this enrichment pass the automatic.com domain (and its api./developer. subdomains) 301-redirects to automattic.com, the unrelated WordPress company, so no live API, documentation, or developer surface remains to harvest. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio lead.

providers.name: AutoTrader.com
providers.description: AutoTrader.com is an American online automotive marketplace headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, and owned by Cox Automotive. Launched in 1997, it connects car buyers and sellers by aggregating listings for new, used, and certified pre-owned vehicles from franchise dealers, independent dealers, and private sellers. The site provides vehicle search and comparison, pricing and valuation tools, financing and trade-in estimates, dealer reviews, and lead-generation connections between shoppers and dealerships. It is a consumer-facing marketplace and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Baicai
providers.description: Baicai (白菜二手车, "Baicai Used Cars") is a Chinese used-vehicle trading platform operating a new-retail model that pairs online used-car marketplaces with offline chain "used-car supermarket" stores. Vehicles listed on the platform are inspected by third-party agencies (100+ point checks that exclude major accident, water-damaged, and fire-damaged cars) and carry a return guarantee plus a warranty on major components. The business was spun out of and operates under 58.com (via Tianjin 58 Cloud Car / 天津五八云车) and became independently operated in 2021. It received early seed backing from Ribbit Capital. Baicai is a consumer-facing marketplace and does not publish a public developer platform, API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and public web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Belanjaparts
providers.description: Belanjaparts is an Indonesian e-commerce platform for automotive spare parts, operating primarily as a mobile application with a searchable catalog of vehicle components, user accounts, shopping cart, order tracking, and location-based services. It serves the automotive aftermarket retail sector and is backed by 500 Global. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer, API, or integration surface at this time (consumer app and website only).

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: Carsome
providers.description: Carsome is Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, with operations across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Singapore. The company runs an online marketplace where consumers can sell, buy, and finance pre-owned vehicles, combining a consumer-facing storefront with B2B dealer auctions, vehicle inspection and certification, logistics, insurance, and financing services. Carsome is a venture-backed technology company (a regional unicorn) counted among the portfolio of 500 Global. No public developer program, API documentation, or API surface has been found; this profile remains a company/lead record awaiting any published API.

providers.name: Cazoo
providers.description: Cazoo was a UK online used-car retailer founded in 2018 by Alex Chesterman, offering a direct-to-consumer platform to buy, sell, and finance used cars fully online with home delivery. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange via a SPAC merger in 2021 before restructuring and entering administration in 2024; its consumer marketplace brand was subsequently sold. Cazoo was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, General Catalyst, and Sapphire Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment: the site is behind bot protection (HTTP 429) and no /.well-known/ discovery documents are published. Sector: ecommerce / automotive retail.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Exide Technologies
providers.description: Exide Technologies is a global producer and recycler of lead-acid batteries used in transportation and industrial applications, serving automotive, motive power, network power, and other markets. Headquartered in Milton, Georgia, the company operates manufacturing and recycling facilities worldwide. No public developer APIs have been identified; ordering and product data are provided through B2B portals and distributor channels.

providers.name: FlightCar
providers.description: FlightCar was a United States peer-to-peer car-rental marketplace built around airport travel, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating company behind the name and no API surface of any kind. The domain flightcar.com is registered but publishes no A, AAAA or MX records, resolves to no host, and sits on Njalla privacy nameservers with a SOA serial dated 2026-07-18; the api, developer and docs subdomains do not resolve; there is no GitHub organisation at github.com/flightcar; and no first-party client library exists on npm or PyPI. The Internet Archive shows the consumer site returning 200 through May 2016 and an Internal Server Error by July 2017, with no successful captures in 2017 or 2018. FlightCar is therefore carried in the network as a defunct company retained for portfolio-graph and historical continuity rather than as an active API provider, and should not be re-queued for artifact enrichment.

providers.name: Freescale Semiconductor
providers.description: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc. was an American semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Austin, Texas, created in 2004 from the spin-off of Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector. Freescale designed and produced embedded processing hardware — microcontrollers (Kinetis, S08), i.MX applications processors, ColdFire and QorIQ/PowerPC communications processors, digital signal processors, RF, analog, and sensor products — for the automotive, networking, industrial, and consumer markets. In December 2015 Freescale merged with NXP Semiconductors in a roughly $11.8B deal and ceased to exist as an independent company; its freescale.com domain now redirects to nxp.com. Freescale was a hardware/silicon company, not a web-API provider: it published no public REST/HTTP API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Frontier Car group
providers.description: Frontier Car Group (FCG) was a Berlin-based startup, founded in 2016, that built, launched, and operated online and offline used-car marketplaces across high-growth emerging markets including Nigeria, Mexico, Chile, Pakistan, Indonesia, India and Poland, offering vehicle inspections, pricing guides, financing, warranties and insurance. OLX Group (Prosus/Naspers) invested up to $400M at a $700M valuation in 2019 and folded FCG into its OLX Autos brand; the Berlin operations were shut down in 2021 and Prosus later moved to exit the car-classifieds business. As of this enrichment pass the frontiercargroup.com domain no longer resolves (registered and ACTIVE through 2027 but serving no DNS A/NS records), the api.frontiercargroup.com host does not resolve, and the company publishes no developer, API, documentation, or other machine-readable surface. Originally surfaced as a Partech portfolio lead.

providers.name: Garaji
providers.description: Garaji was an online auto-services marketplace based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, founded in 2018, that connected car owners with local workshops for routine maintenance and repairs. Customers selected a service and a vetted garage, and a Garaji valet or tow truck collected the vehicle, delivered it to the workshop, and returned it once work was complete. Garaji was a 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) portfolio company. The company is permanently closed, and its domain garaji.com is now a parked, for-sale listing served via GoDaddy/Afternic with no live product or developer surface. This profile is retained as a defunct portfolio-lead record; there are no APIs or developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Harley-Davidson
providers.description: Shop the Official Harley-Davidson site for new and used motorcycles, genuine parts and apparel. Locate a dealer or take a test ride. Harley-Davidson does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Illinois Tool Works
providers.description: Illinois Tool Works (ITW) is a Fortune 500 global multi-industrial manufacturer of value-added consumables and specialty equipment with related service businesses across automotive OEM, food equipment, test and measurement, electronics, welding, polymers and fluids, construction products, and specialty products. ITW does not publish a public API or developer program. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Jjgmachining
providers.description: JJG (JJG Aero Pvt Ltd, JJG Machining Pvt Ltd, and JJG Special Processing Pvt Ltd) is a precision contract-manufacturing group founded in 2004 that produces machined components for the aerospace, automotive, and industrial sectors. It offers 2-5 axis CNC machining alongside high-volume turned and turn-mill parts in ferrous, aluminum, copper alloys, and titanium, backed by 30+ NADCAP-approved special processes such as electroplating, anodizing, paint, and NDT. This is a physical manufacturing company with no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API artifacts; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record only.

providers.name: Joyride
providers.description: Joyride was a mobile audio service that made driving more fun and more interesting, offering an in-car audio/entertainment experience for drivers and passengers. Founded by Jeff Chen (co-founder & CEO) and James Zhang (co-founder & CTO), the company raised a seed round from Cowboy Ventures and was subsequently acquired by Google, marking a successful exit. As a consumer mobile application it exposed no public developer API surface, and the product is no longer independently operated following the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Keno
providers.description: Keno is an on-demand, doorstep car-wash and vehicle-care mobile application operating in the United Arab Emirates, billing itself as the "No.1 car wash app in the UAE". Customers download the iOS or Android app, add their vehicle, select from wash, maintenance, and detailing services (priced by vehicle class from bike to luxury SUV), and a mobile team of "ninjas" arrives at the customer's location to perform the work with a choice of payment methods. Keno is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer mobile application with no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Luxe
providers.description: Luxe was an on-demand valet parking service that let users request a valet through a mobile app to pick up, park, and return their vehicle, operating in San Francisco, Chicago, and New York. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, Luxe is a consumer mobility service with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile records that honest finding.

providers.name: Luxvisions Innovation Limited
providers.description: Luxvisions Innovation Limited is a camera module and imaging technology manufacturer established in March 2018, headquartered in Hong Kong with operations in Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Shangrao, China. The company designs and produces optical camera modules and audio-video integration technology for mobile phones, tablets, PCs and notebooks, automotive systems, AIOT devices, and 3D/ToF VR/AR/MR applications, and states it launched the industry's first triple camera module for mobile phones. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (HongShan Capital) and added to the API Evangelist network. As a hardware/component manufacturer, Luxvisions publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Mekan
providers.description: Mekan (somosmekan.com) is a Latin American software platform serving the automotive sector, with solutions organized around two product lines - Autos (vehicles) and Repuestos (auto parts / spare parts) - to help dealers, parts sellers, and automotive businesses manage and grow their operations. Backed by 500 Global, the company was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network. At the time of enrichment the public surface is a Spanish-language marketing site centered on a "Agenda tu demo" (schedule-a-demo) flow, with WhatsApp and LinkedIn contact channels and no publicly documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Metaldyne Performance Group
providers.description: Metaldyne Performance Group was a leading provider of components for use in powertrain and safety-critical platforms for the global light, commercial, and industrial vehicle markets before being acquired by American Axle.

providers.name: nasn-auto
providers.description: NASN Automotive Electronics Co., Ltd. is a Shanghai-based automotive chassis electronic-control manufacturer founded in 2016, developing brake-by-wire and steer-by-wire systems for smart and assisted driving. Its products include the NBooster intelligent braking system, brushless electric power steering (EPS) controllers, and motion-control solutions for autonomous vehicles. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China, Hillhouse and CATL, NASN has raised roughly $231M and is a Tier-1 supplier pursuing a Hong Kong listing. Surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company; NASN is an automotive hardware manufacturer with no public developer API surface at nasn-auto.com.

providers.name: OneCommand
providers.description: OneCommand was a cloud-based customer marketing and loyalty-automation platform built for automotive dealerships, headquartered in Mason, Ohio. It helped dealers drive service and sales traffic, increase owner retention, and lower marketing costs through data-driven, multichannel outreach across voice, text, email, and direct mail. Its product family included the OneCommand loyalty-automation platform, the Higher Gear CRM, and the TrafficAccelerator service. OneCommand was absorbed into Affinitiv in September 2016, one of four automotive-marketing firms (with TimeHighway.com, Peak Performance and DPS) merged to form that company. The brand is now defunct as an operating surface — onecommand.com and portal.onecommand.com are still fronted by Cloudflare but the origin no longer answers (HTTP 522 on every path probed 2026-08-13), highergear.com no longer connects, and onecommand.net and trafficaccelerator.com resolve to parked landing pages. OneCommand never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation, and the acquirer's site (affinitiv.com) publishes none either.

providers.name: OneSwoop
providers.description: OneSwoop is a UK car-buying and new-car price-comparison website, founded in 1999 and based in Liverpool, England, that lets consumers compare prices on brand-new cars and buy them online at a discount. It operates as a consumer-facing e-commerce and comparison property and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDK surface. Backed historically by Insight Partners and other venture investors, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Padminivna
providers.description: Padminivna (padminivna.com resolves to Padmini VNA Mechatronics Ltd.) is an automotive component manufacturer established in 1991, specializing in innovation and manufacturing of technologies for the auto components industry across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles (M&HCV, LCV), two- and three-wheelers, tractors, and off-road vehicles. Its offerings span ICE, hybrid, and EV powertrains plus sensors and agnostic technologies, with a focus on fuel efficiency, quality, and environmental sustainability. Surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners; the public site exposes only a vendor portal and employee login and publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Penske
providers.description: A diversified transportation services conglomerate operating truck leasing, logistics, automotive retail, and professional motorsports across North America. Penske Corporation spans Penske Truck Leasing (full-service leasing, rental, and contract maintenance), Penske Logistics (supply chain management, warehousing, distribution, dedicated contract carriage), Penske Automotive Group (retail automotive dealerships in the US, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand), and Team Penske (motorsports). The corporate parent has 73,000+ employees and approximately $43B+ in consolidated revenue. Customer self-service is delivered through web and mobile portals (Penske Fleet Insight, Penske Truck Leasing app, Penske Truck Rental); Penske does not publish a public developer API or partner integration portal. Penske Automotive Group is the publicly traded subsidiary (NYSE - PAG).

providers.name: Prodigy Software
providers.description: Prodigy Software was a San Francisco-based provider of cloud-based automotive retail software, offering a SaaS digital-retailing platform that let car dealerships move the sales process online (web-store services, deal structuring, and financing workflows). Founded in 2015 by Marty Hu and Michia Rohrssen, it raised seed funding from Battery Ventures, SV Angel, 8VC, and CrunchFund, and was acquired by Upstart Holdings in March 2021. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain is parked.

providers.name: RedCap
providers.description: RedCap is an automotive dealer service software company that built an on-demand vehicle pickup-and-delivery, loaner, and shuttle platform for dealership fixed-operations (service) departments — offering live vehicle tracking, automated dispatching, at-home loaner contracting, on-demand parts fulfillment, and Uber-integrated shuttle coordination that plug into a dealership's existing DMS and service tools. Backed by Uncork Capital, RedCap was acquired by Solera and is now operated as Solera Service Suite; its former site (getredcap.com) redirects to the Solera Service Suite product. RedCap does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Rimac
providers.description: Rimac Group is a Croatia-based holding company bringing together exclusive hypercars and advanced electrification technology. Its portfolio spans Bugatti Rimac (the hypercar joint venture behind the all-electric Rimac Nevera), Rimac Technology (design, engineering and production of EV components — battery systems, powertrains, battery management systems and electronic control units supplied to OEMs including Porsche, Hyundai, BMW and others), and Verne (autonomous urban mobility / robotaxi). Rimac is a B2B automotive and electrification supplier and vehicle manufacturer; it does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: roadster
providers.description: Roadster was a Palo Alto digital automotive retail commerce platform (its Express Storefront let dealers sell and finance vehicles fully online) that was acquired by CDK Global in 2021 and folded into CDK's automotive digital-retailing suite. The roadster.com domain now serves CDK Global's Automotive Digital Retailing product and no longer exposes a standalone Roadster developer portal, API reference, or public API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public API artifacts are discoverable.

providers.name: roxmotor
providers.description: ROX Motor (roxmotor.com) is a Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturer, a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, best known for the ROX 01 electric off-road SUV. It is a consumer automotive brand with no public developer API surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe. The site is hosted on Tencent Cloud and was not reachable from the enrichment environment for content search.

providers.name: Symbio Robotics
providers.description: Symbio Robotics is an AI industrial-automation company founded in 2014 and based in Emeryville, California. Its flagship product, SymbioDCS, is a robot-agnostic middleware and Python programming framework that lets automation teams build, deploy, and continuously improve AI-driven assembly applications on existing factory robots. Symbio has publicly worked with automakers including Ford, Nissan, and Toyota to speed transmission and vehicle assembly. SymbioDCS is deployed on-premises inside manufacturing lines rather than offered as a public web API; as of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, SDK/package registry presence, MCP server, or API surface, and its former web domains (symb.io, symbiorobotics.com) now resolve to parked/for-sale landing pages.

providers.name: Toyota Connected
providers.description: Toyota Connected is Toyota Motor Corporation's global connected mobility technology arm, building the data, telematics, and software platforms that power Toyota and Lexus connected vehicle services worldwide. The group operates as a federation of regional subsidiaries — TOYOTA Connected Corporation (Japan), Toyota Connected North America (TCNA, Plano, Texas), TOYOTA Connected Europe (TCEU, United Kingdom), TOYOTA Connected India (TCIN), TOYOTA Connected Asia Pacific, and Toyota Tsusho Connected Middle East — and runs Toyota's Mobility Service Platform (MSPF) and the Drivelink telematics backbone behind Safety Connect, Service Connect, Remote Connect, Destination Assist, Wi-Fi Connect, and the "Hey Toyota" in-vehicle voice assistant. TCNA reports surpassing five million connected customer calls across Toyota and Lexus and runs Toyota's Big Data Center for connected-vehicle data. KINTO — Toyota's mobility services brand for car subscription, car-sharing, ride-hailing, and carpooling (KINTO One, KINTO Flex, KINTO Share, KINTO Ride, KINTO Join) — sits adjacent in Toyota's mobility portfolio and is powered by KINTO Technologies on AWS. Toyota exposes developer portals at developer.eig.toyota.com (Toyota API Portal covering TMC, TMNA, TEMA, TFS, NAMC, and other entities) and developer.toyotaconnected.eu (Toyota Connected EU API services, including Telematics and Vehicle APIs documented with Swagger/OpenAPI), but access is gated to partners and internal Toyota teams — no public, unauthenticated OpenAPI specifications are published. Third-party access to Toyota vehicle data for individual developers is typically brokered through partners such as Smartcar and High Mobility rather than directly via Toyota's own portals.

providers.name: TRED
providers.description: TRED is a Seattle-based peer-to-peer online marketplace for buying and selling used cars, founded in 2011 and backed by Techstars, Maveron, Lowercase Capital, and Founders' Co-op. The platform let private buyers and sellers list vehicles, ask questions, schedule concierge-delivered test drives, and complete financed purchases online, with concierges compensated on customer-service reviews rather than sales commission. The tred.com domain now resolves to Cox Automotive / Autotrader infrastructure, indicating TRED has been absorbed into Cox Automotive; it operates as a consumer web product with no public developer program, API, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: tuhu
providers.description: Tuhu (途虎养车) is a Chinese online-to-offline automotive services platform founded in 2011 and headquartered in Shanghai. Through its app, website, and network of franchised and self-operated workshops it sells tires and provides car maintenance, repair, and related aftermarket services to consumers across China. Tuhu is publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (9690) and counts Qiming Venture Partners among its investors. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; enrichment probes found no public developer API, open platform, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tuhu Car
providers.description: Tuhu Car is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: VR Motion
providers.description: VR Motion Corp develops virtual-reality driver-training simulation systems, marketed under its RealDrive product, delivering true-to-life driving simulations that the company says achieve over 70% greater skills retention than traditional training. It serves commercial fleets, last-mile delivery operations, first responders, and driving schools. VR Motion is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer API, docs, SDK, or developer portal, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Genuine Parts Company
providers.description: Genuine Parts Company is a Fortune 500 service organization engaged in the distribution of automotive replacement parts (the parent of NAPA Auto Parts), industrial replacement parts, and electrical materials and electronic components.

providers.name: NIO
providers.description: NIO is a Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer and technology company that develops smart electric vehicles, battery swap technology, and related autonomous driving and connectivity services. NIO provides developer APIs for vehicle data, energy services, and connected car features.

providers.name: Aleris
providers.description: Aleris was a global producer of rolled aluminum products serving the aerospace, automotive, building and construction, and other industrial end-use markets. Founded as IMCO Recycling and later renamed Aleris International, the company operated manufacturing plants across North America, Europe, and Asia. Aleris was acquired by Novelis Inc. (a subsidiary of Hindalco Industries) on April 14, 2020 for approximately $2.8 billion. The company's primary product lines included aluminum sheet, plate, and engineered products for demanding applications such as aerospace structures and automotive body panels. As a manufacturing-focused business, Aleris did not maintain a public developer API program, but engaged in B2B EDI integrations with major customers and suppliers across its supply chain.

providers.name: MisMar
providers.description: MisMar (مسمار) is a Saudi Arabian automotive maintenance and repair platform that connects vehicle owners with certified service centers. It runs a consumer mobile app (B2C) alongside a Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) platform and Workshop Management System (WMS) that digitize fleet management, order processing, and workshop operations for business (B2B), government (B2G), and insurance partners. Services span fault diagnostics, accident restoration, oil and battery and tire changes, periodic maintenance, car wash, and protective treatments across 45+ Saudi cities, with at-home or center-based delivery and warranty coverage. MisMar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is currently published.

providers.name: PACCAR
providers.description: PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture, and customer support of premium light, medium, and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF nameplates. PACCAR also designs and manufactures advanced diesel engines, provides financial services and information technology, and distributes truck parts related to its principal business.

providers.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
providers.description: The world's largest automobile manufacturer by production volume, producing a wide range of vehicles from sedans and SUVs to hybrids and hydrogen fuel cell cars. Pioneer of lean manufacturing and hybrid technology through the iconic Prius.

providers.name: O'Reilly Automotive
providers.description: O'Reilly Automotive is a Fortune 500 specialty retailer of automotive aftermarket parts, tools, supplies, equipment, and accessories serving both do-it-yourself customers and professional service providers. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for O'Reilly Automotive.

providers.name: Penske Automotive
providers.description: Penske Automotive Group is a Fortune 500 diversified international transportation services company that operates automotive and commercial truck dealerships principally in the United States, Canada, and Western Europe. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Borqs
providers.description: Borqs Technologies Inc. is a global Internet of Things (IoT) platform solution provider delivering customizable, differentiated and scalable smart-connected IoT software, hardware and cloud-service platforms. Founded in 2007, Borqs is a Google-licensed Android and Android Wear partner with R&D centers in the U.S., India and China, and debuted publicly on Nasdaq (BRQS) in August 2017. Its BorqsWare platform powers smartphones, tablets, wearables, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), M2M and smart-appliance solutions, and in 2021 it expanded into solar and energy storage systems (ESS) via its Holu Hou Energy acquisition. Borqs is now a Sasken Group company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published; this profile carries company identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: GM OnStar
providers.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. providers.name: Hyundai Bluelink
providers.description: Hyundai Bluelink is Hyundai Motor America's connected vehicle service for Hyundai owners, providing remote vehicle control, vehicle status and diagnostics, navigation and route services, safety and security features, and EV-specific charging and climate management. Bluelink is delivered to owners through the MyHyundai with Bluelink mobile app (iOS and Android), the in-vehicle infotainment head unit, the owner web portal at owners.hyundaiusa.com, and connected smart-home and voice integrations (Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, smartwatch apps). Feature sets vary by model year and subscription tier — typically Bluelink, Bluelink+, and Bluelink Connected Care / Remote / Guidance bundles — and include remote start with climate, remote door lock/unlock, remote horn and lights, vehicle finder, stolen vehicle recovery and SVI, automatic collision notification, SOS emergency assistance, monthly vehicle health reports, destination search (powered by Google), in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot (via AT&T on supported models), and EV-specific remote charge start/stop, charge schedule, charge-level monitoring, and pre-conditioning. Bluelink is a consumer-facing, owner-authenticated service. Hyundai does not publish a public developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API keys for third-party integration with Bluelink vehicle endpoints; access is limited to authenticated owners through Hyundai's first-party apps and to enterprise partners under contract (fleet, insurance telematics, charging networks, smart-home platforms). A community ecosystem of reverse-engineered, unofficial Python and Node.js clients (Hyundai-Kia-Connect/hyundai_kia_connect_api, Home Assistant integrations, Bluelinky) is used by enthusiasts and home automation users, but these are not endorsed, supported, or governed by Hyundai and may break at any time.
